Thick and bloodied, this fleshy sack is plump and fresh.
This stone disc is carved with circular runes and pictographs.
Githyanki actually do have a comedy culture, and it's this: they attack anyone who makes them the butt of a joke.

'When the scissors cut and slicey
They snick and titter ever so nicely.' - Nursery Rhyme
Warmed by occasionally wiggling infernal toes.
A blueprint of the Open Hand Temple.
A human heart, carefully cut from the chest. coagulating blood slowly drips from an artery.
Filled with scholarly texts from across Faerûn - with a few tawdry heroic tales in the mix.
This fang stinks of rotting flesh and death - the remnants of this worg's many hunts.
A humanoid brain - alive and in perfect condition - suspended in cerebrospinal fluid.
A small collection of various tinctures and tonics.
An unsettling but charming drawing of several zombies holding hands together.

Thanks to their mindless appetite for heat, frost salamanders are often tricked by bronze-forged azers. The azers set a campfire blazing, and the salamanders slither toward it hungrily, only to be ripped apart for their alchemically valuable tongues.
Certain ingredients can be purified until only their essence remains. Due to their esoteric nature, these extracts are often linked to the Feywild.
Pulverised minerals and gemstones, mined and traded by the dwarves of Mirabar, give this bowl its bright glaze.
Shockwave Trap
The cant of the hat is avuncular, but the expression of the wearer is cold, detached.
The cogs of this metal contraption are bent out of shape, the steel sheeting dented and cracked. Still, you can make out two sets of initials embossed into the copper: LDH and YTS.
Crackling, stinging sparks leap from these cinder when you stir them with a finger - but the ashes themselves remain almost unnaturally cold.
Ghastly Bottle
Deals Fire and Thunder damage to nearby objects and knocks them back.
Often hauled about by merchants and mongers.
A fireworks pipe rigged to explode - only not in a festival 'look at the pretty sparklers' sense, but rather in a much more 'oh bugger, what a great big explosion' sense.
Patched up in places and recently re-soled, these boots shine with the care of a loving owner.
Carved enchantments span the length of this supple bow.
Hammered into a fine shape by competent smiths.
Twisted and knobbled in nodes of hardened sap, the grain of this bark manages to be both rough and smooth to the touch.
The chaotic fugue of Timmask-induced confusion is in many ways the exact opposite of Myconid meditation, which is calm, spiritual, and does not involve even a little bit of puzzled drooling.

'One of the goddess Selûne's titles, Moonmaiden, has often been debated among the ecclesiastical. Common symbology certainly rejects the assumption of virginity. More to the point, 'maiden' itself carries some dusty connotations. How about Lunar Lady? Keeps the alliteration, too.' - Margaery Henderplum
One of Oddfire's better inventions, this firework bursts with a gorgeous crackle.

Here the famous elven poet unveils the first review for his theatrical production 'Porklet', about a vacillating man who can't bloody make up his bloody mind to just bloody kill his evil uncle (or so spake the review).
A built-up of soot, dust, and a mysterious blue liquid has settled in every nook and cranny of this alchemical set.
Worgs, unlike phoenixes, do not rise from the ashes - but their savagery does.
One of thousands of feathers adorning a giant eagle, you can only hope this graced an elegant part of the bird, such as the wing, and not an inelegant part, such as the left armpit.
Part 13 of the Basics of Alchemy series by Haskinn Xhesilaphin, a descaled dragonborn who lived a life of difficult pain and commendable selflessness.
This slick oil helps your weapon slip through the tiniest of cracks in an enemy's defences.
Data.TechnicalDescription: Coat your weapon to receive a +2 bonus to <LSTag Tooltip="AttackRoll">Attack Rolls</LSTag> with the oiled weapon.

Data.Description: A staff engraved with a leafy motif, maples and oakleaf winding through a forest going through every stage of life, spring to bare-branched winter.
Ivory with the slightest hint of emerald - and thrumming with magic.
These ground xorn scales would be indistinguishable from a pile of sand, if not for their otherworldly shine.
A knitted toy bear stuffed with soft fur. It has a dimple chin and is stitched with the name Godwillington.
The match glow illuminates two conspirators in a plan to shake up their noble bloodline.
Ghastly Bottle
Though this chest's design is elaborate, the wood is unfinished, as though its maker lost interest partway through.
This blade is sharp and slender as a serpent's fang - and just as likely to inflict a hideous sting.
Native to the Nine Hells, imps barely burn, but once they have perished, their wings turn to ash surprisingly easily.
This box is crammed with all the famous fireworks - popdrakes, squidjins, snapbursters, wogglims, ficklebrights, and dimdopplers. (Warning Flammable!)
Since water is indispensable in creating suspensions, they are commonly linked to that element.
Years of simmering soups and sauces have left the inside of this pot with a seasoned sheen.
A delectable feast perfuming the air with the comfortable aromatic smell of herbs and spices.
Filled with scholarly texts from across Faerûn - with a few tawdry heroic tales in the mix.
Coils of frost spiral against the vial's glass - in hushed environments, you can even hear it crackling.
Data.TechnicalDescription: Coat your active weapon in oil. When you hit a foe, it inflicts <LSTag Type="Status" Tooltip="MAG_FROST">Encrusted with Frost</LSTag> for [1] turns.

Data.Description: A small wicker basket, sweet with the scent of fresh fruit.
A powdery narcotic that gives you a tingly feeling and turns your synapses to paste.
Raphael's expression is flat and unreadable, but underneath bubbles that loquacious and self-satisfied temperament.
Ghastly Bottle
Oh, and how fetching a face! Flawed, flawless. Elegant, hideous. Pained, pleasurable. It seems to fit all such descriptors, and many more besides.
An enormous block of ice, created from nothing but the water in the air.
Data.TechnicalDescription: Climbable and destructible.

Data.Description: Aureate twists in the metal give a sheen like polluted sunlight.
The 'in motion' here is curious. What does the artist mean by that? What could be in motion here, in such a still scene?
Ghastly Bottle
The insides of this hat have clasps, not for gloves or cards, but rather for a portable custard pie gag.
Lowly and poorly fitting on any physique, this garb is of the worst quality.
This liquid solution has the colour of evening.
The syrupy liquid languidly swirling inside this bottle somehow reminds you of a predator lying in wait.
Data.TechnicalDescription: Increases your chance to land a <LSTag Tooltip="CriticalHit">Critical Hit</LSTag>. Replaces effects from other elixirs when drunk.

Data.Description: A small sac harvested from a faintly glowing mushroom. It smells incomprehensibly vile.
Those willing to immerse themselves in savagery often reap a blood-red reward.
Data.TechnicalDescription: Drink to enter a bloodlust. Once per turn when you kill a foe, you gain [1] <LSTag Tooltip="TemporaryHitPoints">temporary hit points</LSTag> and an additional <LSTag Tooltip="Action">action</LSTag>. Replaces effects from other elixirs when drunk.

Data.Description: A spellcaster who cannot maintain their spells is about as useful as a chocolate kettle.
Data.TechnicalDescription: Drink to gain <LSTag Tooltip="Advantage">Advantage</LSTag> on <LSTag Tooltip="Concentration">Concentration</LSTag> saves, and against being <LSTag Type="Status" Tooltip="CHARMED">Charmed</LSTag>. Magic can't put you to sleep. Replaces effects from other elixirs when drunk.

Data.Description: Just the most prettily glowing flower and... animal... skull, look yes it's a bit macabre and gross but it's also pretty, okay?
Rope
A tentative and furtive meeting between the red haired man and a woman in apple-red garments.
Each step taken in Gortash's shoes is a reflection of the man himself: quick, sharp, and terrible.
Sophorific drug. Can be inhaled to induce sleep.
What could have been a simple barrel is covered in silver filigree and encrusted with gems of all sizes, as if the maker had more time than sense.
The process of refining salts gives them a granular texture, causing them to be linked to the element of earth.
This dented piece of black metal has a red shine to it, no matter the lighting. Faint screams echo through your mind whenever you touch it.
Heraldic runes are sewn into the padding of this armour, offering a gift of protection to whoever dons it.

Though a thick coating of astral frost prevents this parasite from squirming, you feel an immense psychic weight writhe and roil within. It has languished in the Sea of Dead Gods for countless millennia - learning, gathering potential. It is something old ready to become new again. It is ready for evolution.
Data.TechnicalDescription: This parasite is capable of evolving you or another illithid-infected companion into a new, more psionically powerful being.

Data.Description: Imbibing a chunky, wood-grain tasting broth of Barkskin will make the drinker's flesh as hard as oak.
Though this stone looks velvety black from afar, you observe a myriad of blue, grey, and purple patterns on its surface the moment you hold it in your hand.
Data.TechnicalDescription: Grants the carrier the ability to see in the dark out to a range of [1].

Data.Description: Contemporary, fresh, and very valuable, this piece is believed by savants on the art scene to be something special, perhaps a masterpiece that will marshal in a new genre-based movement.
Dread Lich Queen Vlaakith, looking, to be fair, a bit silly with some rather juvenile horns and a little goatee.
A browning piece of brain sticks stubbornly to one of the spikes.
One of the few ways for elves to experience sleep. Other methods include taking narcotics and being hit very hard with a chair.
Data.TechnicalDescription: Drink to fall into a 2-turn slumber. Unless interrupted, you gain the benefits of a <LSTag Tooltip="LongRest">Long Rest</LSTag>.

Data.Description: Broken Energy Source
Dark silk traps the throat of this helm.
The smoke coming from ki-rin hair releases a soothing scent, as well as the bulk of its heavenly magic.
It is said that the glimmer in this elixir is the reflection of light on the Weave itself.
Data.TechnicalDescription: Gain an additional Level [1] <LSTag Tooltip="SpellSlot">spell slot</LSTag>. Replaces effects from other elixirs when drunk.

Data.Description: Entirely inconspicuous, save for the circular pattern in which it grew.
Though almost scorching, this stone makes you feel pleasantly cool.
Data.TechnicalDescription: Grants the carrier <LSTag Tooltip="Resistant">Resistance</LSTag> to Fire damage.

Data.Description: The suffusion of psionics through the nervous system is generally a slow, perhaps even generational process, as the gith and duergar might well attest to.
Power radiates from this like heat from the sun.
A faceted stone with little sunrises going off in its hue; redolent of Lathander, he who enriches the dawn with light.
Heavy steel bones and teeth enclose the armour's chest and neck like a grotesque exoskeleton that both swallows and protects the wearer.
Undulations throb through this ooze, giving it the look of a larval sack imbued with hideous animation.
'What do you get when you cross a fiend with a rogue? A thiefling.' - nameless comedian moments before his (perhaps timely) murder.
Delicate twists of magical iron - painstakingly gilded - have been fashioned into these fortifying vambraces.
Her cheeks are filled with a blush that seems altogether unrealistic until you meet someone who is, in fact, permanently embarassed.
Part of an outfit worn by the wizard Tenser when he was inducted into the organisation of eminent wizards called the Circle of Eight.

Vitriols differ from other extracts in that refining them seems to make them accumulate all that is vile. Because of this, many have linked them to the Shadowfell. Still, their use cannot be understated.
The fungal flesh lies desiccated.
Paddle
Shar's endless fervour seems to seep blackly from the pieces of this helm.

Data.TechnicalDescription: A mind flayer barrel.

Data.Description: A stately rendition of Vlaakith, dread lich queen of the githyanki. Her sword is so big it's actually unable to be contained within this image, making it look as if she's got a large engraved pole instead.
Unadorned yet intimidating for that factor, this helm speaks to the quiet nobility and equally quiet dread the Fist inspire.
Linked to her with fell magic, these mushrooms keep Auntie Ethel alive until they are destroyed.
Gyroscopic whispers emanate from the device - gnomish machinery speaks with a metal tongue.
Data.TechnicalDescription: <LSTag Type="Status" Tooltip="BLINDED">Blind</LSTag> a target. If it is a steel watcher or scrying eye, it is <LSTag Type="Status" Tooltip="STUNNED">Stunned</LSTag>, and suffers a -1d6 penalty to <LSTag Tooltip="AttackRoll">Attack Rolls</LSTag>.

Data.Description: Though small, this stone swells with an arcane power that makes you feel hale and safe.
Data.TechnicalDescription: Grants the carrier <LSTag Tooltip="Proficiency">Proficiency</LSTag> in Constitution <LSTag Tooltip="SavingThrow">Saving Throws</LSTag>.

Data.Description: Filled with scholarly texts from across Faerûn - with a few tawdry heroic tales in the mix.
Once used to wet a Gauth's eyes, this slime had mostly dried up before you could extract it. Still, its power remains.
An alchemical concoction practically buzzing with potential energy.
Data.TechnicalDescription: Explodes in a cloud of invigorating energy that <LSTag Type="Status" Tooltip="HASTE">Hastens</LSTag> creatures within.

Data.Description: Staring superciliously, this young child is clad in the finest plate, sheets of steel slotted together expertly.
The sap's dark colour, viscous consistency, and cloying sweetness belie its beneficial potential.
Missing its bottom jaw. And its body.
When visiting mortals in dreams, Shar's hair would curl and twist about her head like strands of inky midnight. If it tickled her nose, the goddess was careful not to show it.
The unicorn's blood is dried to the ivory base, defiling the holy magic of the beast's horn.
When held up to moonlight the lens seems to shift, as if its glass core reacts to the scant light of evening.
Filled with scholarly texts from across Faerûn - with a few tawdry heroic tales in the mix.
Difficult to imagine how the artist got the bloody butterfly to stay there for so long...
Formed out of soft clay and mud, this wing is already starting to fall apart.
A small iron key.
Euphoria distilled into an extremely illegal, synapse-melting package.
It is said the Speedy Lightfeet were the first of many lightning inventions made by Yrre the Sparkstruck. The boots' old, frayed edges zap and crackle with even the slightest movement.
These gloves seem to meld to your skin - supple, snug and dextrous as one could hope for.
Grated and fixable, so the wearer might gulp cool air during a fight.
Beam Concentrator
Gortash's boots are as sinister as the man himself - each step taken in them provides an elegant index for his mind, so quick and sharp and terrible.
Like the truffle it is extracted from, this spirit's vibrant colour and smell seem to entice all kinds of critters.
Made of thin-hammered, bell-like metal, the nearly musical chiming of these boots announces the presence of the wearer.
Ghastly Bottle
Sloop
Broken Energy Source
Banded in dark iron, these gloves are embossed with the brass likeness of an elf against a trio of arrows in flight.
Isobel's boots are haphazardly repaired, and have a humble snug fit for the wearer, snug as strong faith in the chest of a religious devotee.
A small bottle, filled to the brim with arcane energy.
Data.TechnicalDescription: Gain an additional Level [1] <LSTag Tooltip="SpellSlot">spell slot</LSTag>. Replaces effects from other elixirs when drunk.

Data.Description: Tiny veins of gemstone marble the gullet - evidence of the worm's unique (and highly toxic) digestive system.
While crows rend gobbets of flesh from battlefield dead, carrion crawlers prefer the seclusion of sewers and cemeteries for their feasting.
This attire disguises you as a poor soul indebted to Raphael - other debtors in his thrall will not be hostile to you.
A self-portrait of Oskar at work, a bemused smile playing on his lips, as if the very act of mixing paints is a dainty and excellent pleasure.
A wet, pungent heap of dung. Still slightly warm.
Vaporous decoction that absolutely rocks the brainstem.
Connected with teleportation magic to its duplicate, this gate allows those who walk through to emerge from its twin gate.
This hammer has a colourful history - it doesn't honk when you squeeze it, alas.
A portable container woven from dried reeds.
Purple Worms are attracted by sonic vibrations. Drow and duergar settlements erect special arcane barriers to deter the incursion of these frightful monsters.
Lupperdiddle Swires, Gnomish Adventurer, could reportedly jump twenty feet in the air. He was about the size of a bantam hen.
Data.TechnicalDescription: Drink this to triple your <LSTag Type="Spell" Tooltip="Projectile_Jump">Jump</LSTag> distance.

Data.Description: Even glazed over in death, the eye's colour is vibrant and menacing.
The yellowish-green ooze dried to the syringe's long needle gives you the distinct impression that this medical device was never used to heal anyone.
Discorporated from its shape, the tail essence gestures to the futility and endurance of conflict between spellcasters and their more sentient failures.

A demonwight, rotted and infested, tries to breed as quickly as it can. A tiefling womb is best, though others will do in a pinch. In that way the demonwight evokes Bhaalspawn, who are fanatical breeders.
The soothing jade handle stands in stark contrast to the trepan's gruesome tip - a reminder of its intended use.
Carved with a verdigris of rot and recalcitrant demonic fire.
These spores sprint about in lovely cyclic patterns, tiny runners on a fungal track.
Shockwave Trap
Waxy-white slime excretes from the pores of this prehensile tentacle.
Inchoate arcane symbols form and dissolve in the salt grains.
Though consisting mostly of plain rock, these thick scales have a crystalline shine no stone on the Material Plane possesses.
With its harsh, almost arachnid cut and shape, this outfit evokes the spiderlike denizens of the Underdark.
Ironically made of magnolias and concentrated ethanol.
Derived from the eye of a mage-hunting Nothic, this elixir waxes from within with a piercing light.
Data.TechnicalDescription: Drink to increase the effectiveness of your spells. You will gain [1] <LSTag Type="Status" Tooltip="MAG_GISH_ARCANE_ACUITY">Arcane Acuity</LSTag>. Replaces effects from other elixirs when drunk.

Data.Description: Filled with scholarly texts from across Faerûn - with a few tawdry heroic tales in the mix.
Though blood and age have rusted the mechanism, a good twist can still make the blades on this bloodletting device spin.
A stately rendition of Vlaakith, dread lich queen of the githyanki. It seems an awfully impractical sword, but she can probably swing it okay, which is somewhat terrifying.

Thanks to their mindless appetite for heat, Frost Salamanders are often tricked by bronze-forged Azers. The Azers set a campfire or a portable forge blazing, the Salamanders slither toward it hungrily, only to be ambushed and torn asunder.
Intellect devourers are born of the brains of humanoid mind flayer thralls. So what is it, exactly, that you are holding in your hands?
Though the stone's surface surges with flickers of electricity, the lightning never seems to touch your fingers.
Data.TechnicalDescription: Grants the carrier <LSTag Tooltip="Resistant">Resistance</LSTag> to Lightning damage.

Data.Description: A frenzy of tiny mushroom-shaped clouds fizzle and pop on the surface of this sublimate.
The product of a fletcher's fine work, meant to be fired from a bow.
Unadorned yet intimidating for that factor, this helm speaks to the quiet nobility and equally quiet dread the Fist inspire.
Forged by dwarven hands, and prized by all warriors who wish to keep their foe at a distance.
Strangely stiff and symmetrical in costruction, this image has an old-fashioned feel, as if Raphael commissioned something more flattering and the artist refused through a brave, bright protest.
A key with a flower motif.
In his troubled Underdark days, the drow with the heart of gold, Drizzt Do'Urden, often purified nightlight to draw out its luminance. By its light his face was pensive, thoughtful, and too-wise.
Several brains are trapped in this device, gently kept afloat in cerebrospinal fluid.
In between the rust and dents, the chipped paint of a wyrm in flight is barely visible.
For just an instant after opening the container, a pale light that moves through a thousand seasonal colours shines, before vanishing forever.
Two sisters, one alive and a ballerina, the other killed in her crib, dance together framed in malefic smoky reds and oranges.
Upon death, a magma mephit's cardiac system floods with sulphur, cooling and hardening it into a vulcanised geode aglitter with scarlet stone.
The metal of these greaves is comfortably warm against your shins, as though heated by your mere presence.
As royal as taxation.
Don't be fooled by the attractive musky scent these petals produce - these flowers feast on humanoid corpses.
A malty aroma wafts from this hay-coloured brew.
Catching the eye, a few quartzy grains of crystal linger.
A sturdy wooden crate, filled with fresh straw and fruit.
Featherlaced and flexible of sole, these boots have been used to round up - and outrun - many a foe.
Purified through sudden heating, these extracts have become vaporous, and are often linked to the element of air.

One can hardly be called a lord if they aren't dressed as such. A cursory glance at Gorash's finery would reveal intricate garb - a closer look would reveal a maddening attention to even the most minute details of the filigree.
This potion is so light, you feel that if you tossed it high, it might float like a lilypad on the pond of the air.
Data.TechnicalDescription: Drink to gain the ability to <LSTag Type="Spell" Tooltip="Projectile_Fly">Fly</LSTag>.

Data.Description: From hedge wizards to high priests, these elixirs are coveted by spellcasters of any ilk.
Data.TechnicalDescription: Gain an additional Level [1] <LSTag Tooltip="SpellSlot">spell slot</LSTag>. Replaces effects from other elixirs when drunk.

Data.Description: Powders mixed with Baffled Squid ink create a mesmerising burst of colour.
Sloop

Eagles have been known to kill tortoises by gripping them by the shell, taking flight, and dropping them from a great height. No one knows why they do this, because there isn't particularly good eating on a tortoise.
Small parts of Weave stick to this foul-smelling paste, imperceptible to any but the most attuned spellcasters.
A small but sturdy bucket, cleaned and filled with straw and fruit.
Donned by the aristocracy during festivals involving a militaristic component.
Cheerfully dancing motes of bioluminescence, reduced to their fundamental matter.
Stacks of Scrolls
The hairs on your arms stand on end each time you touch this remnant of a once-god.
The lonely tenacity of the Chasm Creeper might go some way to explaining its alchemical properties - strength like that could be useful when harnessed.
Despotic, artistic, and terribly powerful, cloud giants often view themselves as elegant sovereigns over the cruder, more terrestrial giantkin.
Part 11 of the Basics of Alchemy series by Haskinn Xhesilaphin, a descaled dragonborn who lived a life of difficult pain and commendable selflessness.
Several brains are trapped in this device, gently kept afloat in cerebrospinal fluid.
Dread Lich Queen Vlaakith, looking, to be fair, a bit silly with some rather juvenile horns and a little goatee.

Data.DisplayName: Headless zombie in Steel Watcher shell.

Data.Description: Fragments of memory and perception smatter this liquid - a crude constellation of thought.
Data.TechnicalDescription: Drink to probe into the minds of those around you. You will be able to read the thoughts of certain creatures while speaking with them.

Data.Description: One whiff of this sickly-sweet smelling vapour makes the sinuses shrink.
A rank, roiling stench emanates from this alchemical concoction.
Data.TechnicalDescription: Explodes into a virulent cloud that can inflict <LSTag Type="Status" Tooltip="BIBBERBANG_FUMES">Noxious Fumes</LSTag> upon creatures within.

Data.Description: Your basic hill giant is just a landslide with a digestive system.
Were it not for its determination not to melt and a distinguishable (almost human) earlobe, this might well be a normal chunk of ice.
The piece of electrum embedded at the top of this staff is filed to a point so it can 'pierce the Weave itself' - symbolically, at least.
Flowing like a horsetail, black as night.
Get the strands wet and you can almost hear the lovelorn sobs.
The flecks of shimmering crystal suspended within this murky oil make it hum with arcane potential.
Data.TechnicalDescription: Coat your weapon in oil. It gains a +[1] bonus to Damage and <LSTag Tooltip="AttackRoll">Attack Rolls</LSTag>, and overcomes <LSTag Tooltip="Resistant">Resistance</LSTag> to non-magical damage.

Data.Description: The red man finds his apple stolen, and looks about for the culprit.
A skilful smith decorated the wooden handle with a fine golden filigree.
Contrary to popular belief, your standard djinni doesn't grant wishes, unless that wish is to have your nose lopped off.
Benches
Deals Fire and Thunder damage to nearby objects and knocks them back.
Though cold to the touch, this stone makes you feel inexplicably warm inside.
Data.TechnicalDescription: Grants the carrier <LSTag Tooltip="Resistant">Resistance</LSTag> to Cold damage.

Data.Description: A pile of today's issues of the Baldur's Mouth Gazette.
Deliberately splotched with gold patches, this turqouise frame would be worth a good deal on its own to the right collector.
The airily sweet mist makes you light-headed, feeling like you could reach for the sun.
An admittedly flattering painting of Lord Enver Gortash, whose face here has a kind of simeon cunning silhouetted by light.
The red haired man dashes from those who would seize him for his petty crime.
The slightest touch of this stone makes your heart speed up, and the muscles in your legs stretch taut in anticipation.
Data.TechnicalDescription: Increases the carrier's <LSTag Tooltip="MovementSpeed">movement speed</LSTag> by [1].

Data.Description: The back cover of this book proudly proclaims: 'The most famed and comprehensive beginner's guide to all things alchemy, in a beautiful 50th anniversary edition. Now with foreword by Adynn Ilvar.'
Ghastly Bottle

The Lord of Murder wasn't always a lord. He was once just a petty killer. When Bhaal first drew blood in a Baldurian back-alley, it dropped to the ground and lingered. When he ascended, this dried blood-drop grew, warped - and became sharp.
This gently glowing orb is held by a tangle of roots and vines, some of which must connect to a mechanism nearby.
Kobold's fashion these sorts of wings to their helms when they wear armour - for it emulates the dragons they worship.
Styled in emulation of the famous Devious Knight of the Deeproot Garden.
Gortash's Lordly Gauntlets
The sides of this brass lamp are shinier than the rest, as if they've been repeatedly rubbed.
'Sometimes I just want to feel that spark,' Yrre the Sparkstruck said. 'Feel the lightning course through me.'
These salts have a surprisingly vast colour palette - the yellows of fungus, greens of moss, and blacks and browns of old blood.
Once plucked from the chest cavity of a recent corpse, this flower was dried and mixed with rare salts to enhance its alchemical properties.
These partially burned balsam leaves exude a smoky, sweet fragrance.
All impurities have been burned off these extracts, and so they are logically linked to the element of fire.
This tangle of webs pulses with expectant magic, eager to unfurl at a moment's notice.
And olde worlde Baldurian design.
Several brains are trapped in this device, gently kept afloat in cerebrospinal fluid.
A cloying sweetness rises from the secretion. It simultaneously sharpens your senses and makes bile rise in your throat.
The stench of this rotten flesh has only worsened during its journey through the alchemical process.
This stone gives you and those around you the Steeped in Bliss condition. Resonance Stones heighten emotion in those who stand within their radius.
Strings of dry gristly sinew cling to the attenuated stump of this stinger.
Pegasi hail from Arborea. There they serve elven gods, their wings spread like broad fans over lush gardens, and their feathers bright with blessings and powers of vitality.
Tattered and infested with crawling bedbugs, this shirt was worn by some interred prisoner.
A key with a flower motif, covered in blood.
Bonecaps are found growing upon burial mounds; their alchemical properties are flavoured with proximal death.
Though noticeably smaller than a beholder's, gauth's eyestalks can likewise shoot terrifying rays. Luckily this one has long perished.
This vivid resin gleams with the promise of power.
The metal, gems, and wood are all polished to perfection, as though the chest's fabricator had all the time in the world to make it.
A serpent slithers through the eye socket of a rotting skull, its green slimy skin leaving a trail on the nearby bones.
In his youth, Ketheric Thorm has the same puzzled, ever-curious brow belonging to any kid. Lamentable, that the brow this circlet adorned warped with tragedy and a sick determination over time.
Rendered with sumptuous skill, great gouting bleed seeming to squirt and dribble and spill like wine from drunk lips, the violence impeccable, the tangled quality sublime.
Energy Source
A crate of bleached wood, used to store a variety of vegetables.
This muddy sludge glitters with otherworldly magic.
Data.TechnicalDescription: Cures <LSTag Type="Status" Tooltip="BLINDED">Blinded</LSTag>, <LSTag Type="Status" Tooltip="SILENCED">Silenced</LSTag>, <LSTag Type="Status" Tooltip="PARALYZED">Paralysed</LSTag>, and <LSTag Type="Status" Tooltip="POISONED">Poisoned</LSTag> creatures.

Data.Description: This feather would make the softest duck down feel like hedgehog quills.
The gelid texture of this substance is a reflection of the frost giants who tame equally icy salamanders at the intersection between the Planes of Air and Water.
The piece of electrum embedded at the top of this staff is filed to a point so it can 'pierce the Weave itself' - symbolically, at least.
Filled with scholarly texts from across Faerûn - with a few tawdry heroic tales in the mix.
The gelid texture of this substance is a reflection of the frost giants who tame equally icy salamanders at the intersection between the Planes of Air and Water.
The motion of the shimmering liquid going back and forth in its vial is somnambulant - you know drinking it will bring the comfort of a warm, enveloping blanket.
Data.TechnicalDescription: Drink to fall into a 2-turn slumber. Unless interrupted, you gain the benefits of a <LSTag Tooltip="ShortRest">Short Rest</LSTag> and regain all 1st and 2nd Level <LSTag Tooltip="SpellSlot">spell slots</LSTag>. If you are awoken before the duration expires, the effects will not apply.

Data.Description:
The origin of the nothic curse is one-eyed Vecna, the undead lich and master of secrets.

Nothics themselves do not remember their former lives as wizards - but their eyes can still be distilled for the benefit of spellcasters.
These gauntlets spark with unfinished, yet still potent devillish magic - indicative of a cancelled blacksmith's commission.

No surprise that Lolth's Candles lead travellers in the Underdark, given that their namesake is a goddess of deceit as well as spiders and shadows. Worse, distilled, they even blind and poison the unwary.
A suspicious arm rises from one of these barrels.
This tough, inflexible reed grows in waterside clusters and makes for a fine building material.
The Netherbrain's will made manifest. Anything that would disrupt the Grand Design is mistaken - mistakes are to be corrected.
A thick miasma exuded by the bone shards of a dead god. For some inexplicable reason, it makes you feel safe.
A rogue's favourite toy.
The roots of the common mugwort weed can be dried and crushed to create a powder that looks unassuming, but is full of potential.
Whatever corpse this fetid cancer was once attached to has long rotted away, leaving only its affliction behind.
A polished wooden easel, speckled with copious dollops of paint in a rainbow of colours.
An aged spear, its steel head nicked by the blows of a dozen battles.
Though textured like half-frozen honey, this liquid flows as effortlessly as mercury.
Data.TechnicalDescription: Your <LSTag Tooltip="MovementSpeed">movement speed</LSTag> can't be reduced by <LSTag Type="Status" Tooltip="DIFFICULT_TERRAIN">Difficult Terrain</LSTag> or spells. You can't be <LSTag Type="Status" Tooltip="PARALYZED">Paralysed</LSTag> or <LSTag Type="Status" Tooltip="RESTRAINED">Restrained</LSTag>. Replaces effects from other elixirs when drunk.

Data.Description: Linked to her with fell magic, these mushrooms keep Auntie Ethel alive until they are destroyed.
Everything moves strangely in the Feywild, from rivers to behaviours. It's a mercurial place, where the magical and physical can pass permeably through one another.
The saw's teeth are blunt and rusted, it's beautiful metalwork barely visible beneath a layer of black, coagulated blood.
Strangely stiff and symmetrical in costruction, this image has an old-fashioned feel, as if Raphael commissioned something more flattering and the artist refused through a brave, bright protest.
Wearing these boots is like walking on cotton clouds.
'Look, it's perfectly simple. You just coat the person in the oil, like so. Then you strike a match, like s- oh bugger.' - Bufort Iggles, The Unfortunate
Data.TechnicalDescription: On hit, a coated weapon covers its target in oil for 2 turns. Oil-covered targets immolate upon taking fire damage, dealing [1] to everyone and everything nearby.

Data.Description: A small collection of various tinctures and tonics.
Sturdy and well-worn, these boots make a snug fit on any wearer.
Oft planted near graveyards and gifted to the sickest of patients, black oleander is believed to keep necrosis from spreading.
There is an eager, annihilating darkness thrumming within this weapon - it begs to be used.

'It was then that Swires tossed the oil. It splattered the cambion, and all at once its skin of brilliant carmine dulled to dark, a red like cheap wine, and the fiend vented this sound of anguish I almost pitied, for its very affinity for fire was now undone.'
Data.TechnicalDescription: Coat your weapon in an oil that transforms the target's <LSTag Tooltip="Resistant">Fire Resistance</LSTag> to Fire <LSTag Tooltip="Vulnerable">Vulnerability</LSTag>. Targets that are <LSTag Tooltip="Immune">Immune</LSTag> to Fire damage are unaffected.

Data.Description: Hammered from an alloy of strong mountain metals.
Tempered in rich oils and beaten until perfect.
Crushed Laculite floats at the bottom of this tincture, infusing the water with the Underdark's mysterious energies.
Gold embroidery covers the inside of the tabard, right over the heart: 'By any means necessary, I will fight the Greater Evil, showing no mercy for the wicked.'
Linked to her with fell magic, these mushrooms keep Auntie Ethel alive until they are destroyed.
The golden slopes of the celestial heavens are filled with angels. Theistic scholars don't know what they do, but whatever it is, they do it holy.
Made from steel hammered thin, these gauntlets are a fine investment for any warrior.
Beautiful as suspended snow, these spores sting your cheeks, set fire to your trachea, and putrefy your lungs.
Data.TechnicalDescription: Airborne, deadly spores that deal [1] to any who inhale them.

Data.Description: 'When I found Carixim, he turned to me, with all those poor people's souls crammed into him, and he... he grinned at me. He said, "I been expecting you, boy."' - Overheard from the smith Dammon
Now and again, a small ball of light flickers in the dark liquid, like the reflection of some alien yet sweet star on the darkest ocean.
Data.TechnicalDescription: Bathe a nearby area in light.

Data.Description: The belief that the Feywild is a dreamy plane of whimsical adventure is folly. The occasional rainbow-coloured glint from this substance could as easily evoke a treacherous oil slick.

Cazador's love of poetry arose after he read one on the naked stomach of a dead child in his homeland. The child was hung from the lowest branch of a tree. Cazador read the poem, and looked at the child, and he knew that here was the artform for him.
Few sounds in the vast Underdark are as eerie as the clacking, echoing chatter of hook horrors - made even worse by the fact that they are usually a warning of even graver dangers to come.
No matter how small, rare, or cute a critter, it will still fill your stomach.
Barrier Generator
Even the slightest sniff of this acidic tincture makes your eyes sting.
Part 9 of the Basics of Alchemy series by Haskinn Xhesilaphin, a descaled dragonborn who lived a life of difficult pain and commendable selflessness.
An elaborate chest made from strange metals and wood you've never seen before.
Shockwave Trap
The blood on this finger has clotted in strange swirling patterns - like a grotesque facsimile of cumulus clouds.

Abstract and a little disturbing for that, this portrait of Bane tries to depict his mastery of tyrannt using harsh, thick lines. Furthermore it renders him half-nude, oddly humanising, perhaps a nod to Bane's mortal origins before he ascended to godhood.

Data.DisplayName: Frameless Portrait of Ketheric and Melodia Thorm
Data.Description: Here, reclining and standing respectively, their hands clasped and regal, even stentorian, are a husband and wife at the height of their accomplishment and devotion.
Etched with a small bouquet of filigree near the heel, these boots were made by a smith with a flair for decoration.
Inhaling the wrong spores can dissolve even the sharpest intellect into fizzing confusion.
Data.TechnicalDescription: Lob this vaporous decoction to <LSTag Type="Status" Tooltip="TIMMASK_SPORES">Befuddle</LSTag> nearby foes.

Data.Description: A sheen of clear poison coats this fang, like a wasp's autumnal stinger.
Before your eyes, the elixir firms into a tough, striated twig, then it liquefies once more.
Data.TechnicalDescription: Drink to increase your <LSTag Tooltip="ArmourClass">Armour Class</LSTag> to 16. Replaces effects from other elixirs when drunk.

Data.Description: Remember this, as you hold these heavenly sparks: any creature that takes a role in the death of a unicorn risks incurring divine wrath.

She prayed for words and received silence. She prayed for intimacy and slept alone. She prayed for fruit and ate charcoal. She prayed for death and wanted to live. Then she grew older, and received things she'd wanted.
Still she prayed.
Toughened metal boots, highly insulated with heavy leather and padding for use in any and all elements.
This tough, inflexible reed grows in waterside clusters and makes for a fine building material.
Slightly sticky to the touch, these boots have excellent grip.
Touching a little of the substance to your lips, you begin to hear muffled pulses of  sound - daubs of thoughts belonging to those nearby.
If Iggwilv's Demonomicon has the right of it, all oozes are the spawn of the Faceless Lord, the demon tyrant Juiblex - it also cites the useful motion-based alchemical properties of the substance.
Beneath its vial of glass the liquid floods with colour, goes translucent, and becomes colourful once more - a pretty fluctuation.
Data.TechnicalDescription: Drink this elixir to spot Invisible creatures. Replaces effects from other elixirs when drunk.

Data.Description: Gazing glassily up at you, bereft of humanity, this bulbous eye evokes the gruesome curse of the nothics. For they were not always monsters, but wizards who groped too greedily for power.
Difficult to imagine how the artist got the bloody butterfly to stay there for so long...
A soft ball of green slime. Thick drops slide down your fingers, stinging your skin.
Stimulates the pineal gland in the brain, unlocking malevolent power.
Data.TechnicalDescription: Gain <LSTag Type="Status" Tooltip="ALCH_ELIXIR_TADPOLE">Psionic Weakening</LSTag> and <LSTag Type="Status" Tooltip="ALCH_ELIXIR_TADPOLE_ADVANTAGE">Psionic Enrichment</LSTag>. Replaces effects from other elixirs when drunk.

Data.DisplayName: Portrait of a Bored Girl (Playing Music)
Data.Description: Even with the addition of her lute, the C chord strumming out sensuously from the canvas to the ear, this young woman still looks immensely, disconsolately bored.

Data.TechnicalDescription: A mind flayer crate.

Data.Description: There are some scholars who believe the demonwight a sort of boogeyman; adults believe that, but children can be harder to convince when the wind is howling without, and the shutters of their windows seem constantly to creak, and is being slowly prised open...
Swan-necked and very lovely withal, this particular blush is keenly embarrased - perhaps she dind't much care to be depicted in paint.
Large foul-smelling barrel.

Here a small pun is employed in the title; the red haired man who has stolen the apple for the child perhaps has reservations or 'qualms' about doing so, yet this word contains 'alms' which is a synonym for charitable donation.

When a feckless  spellcaster attempts to create life and bungles it, the result is a gremishka. Spiteful and malformed, gremishkas hold a particular loathing for practitioners of the arcane arts, a dark reflection of typical parental love.
Filled with scholarly texts from across Faerûn - with a few tawdry heroic tales in the mix.
Created using the dried gills of the rogue's morsel mushroom, this powder smells surprisingly sweet.
A clown's hand, nastily cut from the wrist. Some face-paint dapples the fingertips.
A master of sonnets and plays about ambition, supernatural tensions with the natural world, avarice, love, and moving bushes.
Many view ki-rin as heralds of good fortune, and for good reason - even the tiniest strand of their hair holds a wealth of benevolent magic.
Shiny with oil, these boots have an earthy, pleasant smell and are tied with high-quality leather laces.
Jimmied up to the throat with dark powder, popdrakes give off a smell like singeing dragon breath.
Broken Energy Source
Entirely inconspicuous, save for the circular pattern in which it grew.
This longsword never dulls, although an observer may notice it quietly drinks the blood of slain enemies.
A malty aroma wafts from this hay-coloured brew.
Three concentric lenses give a clear view of every tooth, hair and wrinkle of a dried-out, limp mind flayer tadpole.
Ghastly Bottle
Harrowing and beautiful and terrible. What does it condemn, though?
Though green miasma practically drips off this stone, the pebble itself emits a soothingly sweet aroma.
Data.TechnicalDescription: Grants the carrier <LSTag Tooltip="Resistant">Resistance</LSTag> to Acid damage.

Data.Description:
Let hill and hollow be a door
To screams that last forevermore.
The oil refined from these ashes will act as a catalyst for the prettiest bursts of furnace-hot flame.
The soft and supple leather glides over your skin. Wearing them feels like running barefoot.
In his grouchier years as a scholarly wizard, Otiluke would lob his famous freezing sphere at overeager university students rather than actually stoop to giving them lectures.
Data.TechnicalDescription: Throw to cast <LSTag Type="Spell" Tooltip="Projectile_FreezingSphere_Hurl">Otiluke's Freezing Sphere</LSTag>, wreaking frosty havoc on the battlefield.

Data.Description: Symbols for the eight schools of magic fluctuate in this oil - one by one appearing and dissolving in the oil, as if devoured.
Data.TechnicalDescription: Coat your weapon in oil. Its targets receive a [1] penalty to <LSTag Tooltip="AttackRoll">Spell Attack Rolls</LSTag> and <LSTag Tooltip="DifficultyClass">Spell Save DC</LSTag>, and <LSTag Tooltip="Disadvantage">Disadvantage</LSTag> on <LSTag Tooltip="SavingThrow">Saving Throws</LSTag> for maintaining <LSTag Tooltip="Concentration">Concentration</LSTag> for [2] turns.

Data.Description: Gortash's reflectoguard applies a condition that reflects all incoming projectiles back at their source.
Barrier Generator
Barrier Generator
Rippling with current and the plashing of silver fish just under the surface, the river flows somnolently onward.

Ice mephit ears boast the alchemical property of nullifying fire resistance. Though completely useless to the mephits itself, they seem to revel in the thought of imparting their own vulnerabilities onto others.

Although they abhor violence, myconids boast both poisonous gas pockets and pulverising limbs - a clear indicator that the harsh reality of the Underdark has equipped them with defensive capabilities, should that abhorrence slacken.
It is one of life's small ironies that the first step in creating an Elixir of Fire Resistance includes burning its main ingredient.
These tiny slivers of copper glisten when illuminated - almost like miniature bolts of lightning.
Molten earwax clings to the ashes, turning the whole into a sticky goo.
In this transmogrified state, Belladonna loses its toxic properties, gaining instead an engrossing, perception-enhancing characteristic.

Touching this amulet's centrepiece, you are imbued with a vision of woven strands, and the strands coming apart and holding true and firm over your friends, like shields banded in a haze of golden light.
Dripping wet, these boots squelch uncomfortably around your toes with every step.
As well travelled as any set of boots on Toril.
This ivory quill could be mistaken for a plain eagle feather, if not for the power pulsating off it in waves.
Its blades have been worn dull from years of use.
Grant nearby Steel Watchers an additional <LSTag Tooltip="Action">action</LSTag> with roiling arcana.

Ironically, the blinding property of behir scales mirrors the short-sightedness of the storm giants who created the first behirs - fashioned from serpentine lightning, they did not remain subordinate to their giant masters for long.
Though no bigger than a fist, this stone makes you feel strangely grounded.
Data.TechnicalDescription: Grants the carrier <LSTag Tooltip="Resistant">Resistance</LSTag> to Thunder damage.

Data.Description: Thanks to the finger's vast size, each spot of fungus, mud, and flesh stuck beneath its fingernail is agonisingly clear.
The fungal flesh lies desiccated.
The piece of electrum embedded at the top of this staff is filed to a point so it can 'pierce the Weave itself' - symbolically, at least.

'Trundling, mashing, mincing, crushing, grinding, blasting, biting! Hear their peeling thunder, their roaring flames, their clicking, whirring, metallic melody, and know that the hellfire engines of Avernus are on the move!' - Edict in Elturel
Her throat sheathed in a truly gargantuan ruffle, this noblewoman regards the onlooker with lips slightly parted, as if attentive or ready to voice some secret.

A tyrant's grip must be one of cool, unforgiving, and intricately realised steel. It cannot budge, cannot falter, no matter the pressure, and its fingertips must deeply pierce those who would struggle against it.
This improvised grenade was handcrafted by skirmisher-devils to be used in infernal combat.
Filled with scholarly texts from across Faerûn - with a few tawdry heroic tales in the mix.

While the painting's title is ostensibly referring to the child in his red hat at the busy market, it is in fact a clever allusion to the red haired man stealing an apple (or colloquially in this part of the word 'red hatter') from a stall.
Even through the thick glass, the arcane energy contained within this bottle makes your fingers tingle.
Data.TechnicalDescription: Gain an additional Level [1] <LSTag Tooltip="SpellSlot">spell slot</LSTag>. Replaces effects from other elixirs when drunk.

Data.Description: House of Hope Engine Console
Often fed with the blood of the fallen, daggerroot is said to help create new victims - a property that only intensifies once the plant has been dried and burned.

An enormous storm was raging the first time Yrre the Sparkstruck left the Underdark. The deep gnome's interest in lightning became at once an all-consuming obsession, and they would spend the rest of their years striving to recreate that storm's power themselves.
While alive, yellow musk creepers feed on humanoid corpses, turning them into zombies, but in the hands of a skilled alchemist, their petals can be used for good.
The visor is splendidly insigniad with gold and silver.

Ceremorphosis eradicates great swathes of the consciousness that came before... but not everything. Touching the staff, a fragment of the Emperor's memory slithers into your brain - you see sea waves foaming into spume, and feel the explorer's exultant joy.

Then the image is gone, like so much silken night under a cut-shade sun.
Here Corellon is not shown as a beautiful golden haired elven God, but as a dark haired elven Goddess, the body mirrored and contorted with a delicious grace and embedded upon maroon muslin.

While the ersatz eye is embedded in your eye socket, you can see through the tiny orb as though it were a normal eye. Can't be removed once inserted.

A hollow bead of white glass, carefully painted to resemble a realistic eye. Its tarnished brass fittings hum with a tinge of magic.
The metal of these greaves is comfortably warm against your shins, as though heated by your mere presence.
A set of runes has been expertly worked into the helmet's filigree. Almost imperceptible - but powerful nonetheless.
A many-sided artefact of blackened iron, engraved with pulsating runes. Something stirs within.
This cumbersome blade looks strong enough to survive journey through all nine Hells.
A volume detailing the many plants found in the Dalelands of north Faerûn.
Found in the Spider Queen's stomach, this robe emanates a sour smell and stings to the touch.
For every drop of blood spilled, a piece of the soul perishes - until nothing remains but regret.
This 'bag' is barely more than a sewn-together old sheet, so worn that any snag could rip it.
Suede covers the palms of these gloves - ensuring a soft, comforting touch for anyone in need of help.
Grimy, discoloured, and revoltingly ugly. Auntie Ethel must have made it herself. Surprisingly, you feel no disgust. Instead it fills you with a longing, as if it's calling out for its like.
Entirely inconspicuous, save for the circular pattern in which it grew.
Though well-preserved, the armour's gleam is somewhat muted - as if half-shadowed, even in brightest day.

Data.DisplayName: Volo's Guide to Spirits and Spectres
Data.Description: The working draft of a book on... spirits?
A deep, dark crack in the wood.
These coins grant the Toll Collector protection against attacks, but will be lost if destroyed.
This ring is missing its gem - or perhaps it's just very invisible.
A subtle accessory prized by purveyors of the covert arts.
A jumbled assortment of planks, lashed together with rope.
A golden blade, exquisitely made and astonishingly sharp.
The exterior of this ring is roughly carved with nonsensical runes.

Yrre the Sparkstruck got their nickname for both their obsession with lightning and the inventions they created, which had the habit of electrocuting both Yrre and any poor observers that got too close.
The point of this spear is blackened and melted - the uneven metal is designed to catch deep in the wounds it creates.
A small leather pouch, sealed tight with an array of purple, yellow and scarlet threads.
Entirely inconspicuous, save for the circular pattern in which it grew.
Each of this amulet's jewels shines like a viper's eyes.
Blessed by the Oak Father himself, this tonic will cure even the most baneful poisons.
Legends say the Giantbreaker earned its name when an elven ranger singlehandedly defeated a score of hill giants. While the ranger's name is long forgotten, Giantbreaker's lives on.
Its owner frequently insisted he didn't need this hand-cut linen square, but his sister kept it to hand in case his allergies kicked up.
Stamped with Shar's own sigil, this helm was worn by the Nightsinger's own crusaders. The darkness within seems deeper than night, somehow.
A cruel and crude blade forged en masse by goblin hordes.
Sending Stone
A thick layer of dust coats the bottom of the lantern. Its glass is cracked, its metal bent beyond repair.
A plain leather bag, cinched at the top with knotted cord.
Bringer of that which it is.
Though caked with mud and grime, the ring smells faintly of lavender. Remarkable, considering where it's been.
Read for Debug Commands.
A many-sided artefact of blackened iron, engraved with pulsating runes. Something stirs within.

This necklace allows the wearer to cast Misty Step.

Made of blue gems unique to a privately-owned mine in Menzoberranzan, this necklace was likely a token of esteem - or perhaps a desperate attempt to win its recipient's mercy.
Damp has seeped through the planks, all but obliterating inscription. The tap is sticky from use.
Owlbear hatchlings are tiny and adorable for the first few tendays of their life. Then they eat you out of house and home. Then they simply eat you.
A hand-like brand stamped into the leather handle obscures the notches that would normally signify a hobgoblin's rank.
Sleek and lightweight, it is said that the Joltshooter was Yrre the Sparkstruck's favourite weapon. They were indifferent towards bows, but the spikes jutting out of it?
Pulverised minerals and gemstones, mined and traded by the dwarves of Mirabar, give this bowl its bright glaze.
A pale green eye, pierced by the twisting branches of a dead tree - the result of a foolhardy woman begging Auntie for a favour.
Though the crossbow's bolts look burning hot, they are pleasantly warm to the touch.
'Lightning is like magic,' Yrre the Sparkstruck once said. 'And what is magic but life itself?'
Blood is smeared across the shield's face, exalting wielders who bear the Absolute's mark.
A simple bag fashioned from a single piece of rough burlap.
The remainder of a spear shaft, snapped cleanly in the middle.
A heavy haft and wide blade belie the speed of this weapon. It parts the air as swiftly as any duelling sabre.
Pulverised minerals and gemstones, mined and traded by the dwarves of Mirabar, give this bowl its bright glaze.
This bright blue flower, picked from a budding sussur tree, exudes a honey-sweet aroma, which turns foul and eventually fades away if the bloom is exposed to sunlight.
Sussur roots extend from this sword's hilt into the blade itself. It yearns to drink magic, silencing every creature it strikes.
Data.TechnicalDescription: <LSTag Type="Status" Tooltip="SILENCED">Silences</LSTag> targets on hit.

Data.Description: The words 'Deliverance. Justice. Vengeance.' are engraved on the base of this sword. They echo in your mind.
A small pebble swings from a length of fishing line tied to this copper ring.
Thread-like vines wriggle along this wooden staff.
This light, flexible staff is of elven make, marked with mithral sigils that channel magic in the blink of an eye.
This very accurate book is packed full of tales of the grimy streets, raucous taverns, and outlandish characters of Baldur's Gate.
Named after the god of martyrs, this amulet seems to shine in the presence of the wearer's blood.
Intricately carved, weathered by water and wind.
Every gem hanging from this necklace is warm to the touch, as if waiting to ignite.
A soft, soothing voice floats from this ring, reciting a prayer over and over.
Cast deep in the Underdark by duergar slaves, the head of this mace is engraved with spiderwebs. It is ice-cold to the touch.
Though carefully stowed away in a bedside chest, this ring is covered in dust and cobwebs.
Entirely inconspicuous, save for the circular pattern in which it grew.
A glob of tree sap studded with dead ants occupies the space where this ring's stone once sat.
The elegant design of this hammer belies its brutal, crushing power. This weapon does not give ground.
Somehow, this axe perpetually feels warm to the touch.
Each cut of this blade shines with the wicked glint of adamantine - a promise for a devastating blow.
This long, slender blade fits perfectly between the ribs of any unsuspecting victim.

Yrre the Sparkstruck intended to give the Spellsparkler to Lenore, a cleric of Mystra and old lover. But when the gnome returned to the cleric's tower, they found it empty - inhabited only by dust and abandoned experiments.
The adamantine scales hug your body like a second skin - a heavy, near-impregnable skin.
Live worms wriggle beneath the crumbling surface of this half-rotten staff. Merely touching it fills you with a wave of unbearable nausea and a strange longing, as if it's calling out for its like.
A forest of mushrooms sprout from Nere's skin, eyes, and open mouth, cheerily feeding on clotted blood.
Worn by Shar's most loyal zealots, the mere sight of it strikes fear in the heart of even the bravest of souls.
Streaks of tendon and sinew cling to the animal skull lashed atop of this wooden staff.
This pure silver key was found on the corpse of a worshipper of Selûne.
The back bears an inscription under a delicate crescent moon. 'You're a novice no more, Robin. Only right you should carry a little of our Lady's light with you.'

Become invisible for 1 minute. Attacking or casting spells ends the condition.

You'd think this bottle was empty but for the sound of sloshing liquid from within.
The perfectly preserved brain suspended in the bubbling liquid is... screaming? Somehow, you can hear it.
This staff pulses with energy, swiftly attuning itself to the beat of your heart.
Though the grip's leather is old and crusty, it shows no signs of wear, and not a single scratch mars the slender blade.
Silent flames surge the length of the blade as soon as it clears the scabbard.
A gawking yellow eye is pierced on this broken spear head.

Grants wearer ability to cast Hail of Thorns.

Whoever previously owned these gloves marked each with a series of thirty superficial scrapes, six per finger. What they indicate is unclear.
Tiny barbs prick the wearer when they're injured, as if urging flight from danger.
A simple bag fashioned from a single piece of rough burlap.
Prideful as he was in life, Nere is just like anybody else in death - mouth slack, eyes bulging, and flesh that is slowly starting to rot.
Once home to an inscrutable machine intelligence, Grym's skull now serves as a simple helm.
Inky notes slash across the margin of this particular scroll, the angle of the handwriting suggesting urgency. Perhaps warning.
The sheen of sussur sap forged into this sickle glows blue, silencing every creature it cuts.
Data.TechnicalDescription: <LSTag Type="Status" Tooltip="SILENCED">Silences</LSTag> targets on hit.

Data.Description: A menacing cackle emanates from this twisted charm. It whispers to bite, to maim, to kill...
The drow inscription on this blade appears to have been recently carved. It translates to: 'Though I have to leave you, I will dance forever in Eilistraee's light.'
These coins grant the Toll Collector protection against attacks, but will be lost if destroyed.
The intricate engravings on this axe's blade and handle make plain the skill of its smith.
Used by the previous owner to access both the Underdark's darkest corners and her own basement, this ring seems to reflect light where there should be none.
A childlike charcoal drawing of three stick figures.
And they shall have Celestia's light, even if we must crack wide the heavens to bring it."
Though ancient and cracked, a powerful divine energy laps from this gem in waves, singeing everything in its path.
Though this rotting chair leg doesn't look like much, every splinter vibrates with barely-contained power.
Someone cut the poor clown's head off. Tendons sweep from the ragged throat like circus wire.

Data.DisplayName: Volo's Guide to Spirits and Spectres (Signed)
Data.Description: Although the draft of this book on spirits is very much a work in progress, it does begin with a heartfelt dedication.
A secret concoction of smokepowder and gnomic mysticism, a single vial of runepowder is more volatile than a whole barrel of smokepowder. Who knows what this much could do...
The dagger's leather grip is stamped with a stag's head - the symbol of the Emerald Enclave.
Two lice still scurry around on the little flap of skin attached to this clump of matted, crusty hair.
Data.TechnicalDescription: Consuming this piece of fey flesh grants a permanent +1 bonus to <LSTag Tooltip="Dexterity">Dexterity</LSTag>.

Data.Description: Rotten rags and mud are the only things keeping this mace together.
A small leather pouch, sealed tight with an array of purple, yellow and scarlet threads.
Unusually heavy. It seems to creak of its own accord.

Time has dampened this spear's sheen, but the centre glows a faint blue. The magic it exudes feels old, terrible... and divine. The spear was given to its previous owner for his unerring loyalty - even after death.
You'd think this bottle was empty but for the sound of sloshing liquid from within.
Data.TechnicalDescription: Turn Invisible. The condition ends early if you attack or cast a spell.

Data.Description: Dirt and rust mar the edges of this spear, but it is deadly all the same.
A small gemstone, dulled by decades of handling by nervous fingers. A small rune has been scrupulously carved into its tip.
Entirely inconspicuous, save for the circular pattern in which it grew.
This bright blue flower, picked from a budding sussur tree, exudes a honey-sweet aroma, which turns foul and eventually fades away if the bloom is exposed to sunlight.
Smoke-like whorls of sussur sap darken the metal of this dagger's blade and silence its victims.
Data.TechnicalDescription: <LSTag Type="Status" Tooltip="SILENCED">Silences</LSTag> targets on hit.

Data.Description: The linked rings crackle with energy just waiting to be released.
A finely crafted silver locket, engraved with the words 'For Papa.'
With a dedication written with an extravagant hand, this book is packed full of tales of the grimy streets, raucous taverns, and outlandish characters of Baldur's Gate.
A bundle of bones and blood - and a soul-piercing demonic presence - is all that remains of the Flind's flail. It would make a decent mace with a particularly nasty bite.
Chunks of fat and leathery meat float in a watery soup.

Data.DisplayName: Taking the Groves Off the Table

Data.Description: Grime covers this necklace, but you can vaguely discern delicate engravings of a moon and harp.
Filled with a nauseating cocktail of beer, spirits, and... something else. The consistency suggests an unpleasant addition.

Data.DisplayName: Volo's Complete Guide to the Behaviour of Nymphs (Signed)
Data.Description: A fawning dedication opens this heavily edited draft of a book that examines the activities of nymphs in GREAT detail.
Strange, incomprehensible whispers emanate from this coin, pervading your mind with rage and despair.
The drow inscription on this blade appears to have been recently carved. It translates to: 'Though I have to leave you, I will dance forever in Eilistraee's light.'
Two lice still scurry around on the little flap of skin attached to this clump of matted, crusty hair.
Data.TechnicalDescription: Consuming this piece of fey flesh grants a permanent +1 bonus to <LSTag Tooltip="Strength">Strength</LSTag>.

Data.Description: Forged from an unfamiliar alloy. Uncommonly rugged.
This splintering cane has struck enough victims to have cracked from overuse.
Runepowder was said to be invented by Gaerdal Ironhand, the protector god of gnomes. A mere 23 vials were needed to repel an assault led by Kurtulmak and his Kobold Delvers.
'Is there anything as beautiful as lightning striking all around you?' Yrre the Sparkstruck said, letting lightning strike all around them.
Even though the embroidered velvet won't help against a sharp blade, wearing it fills you with self-assuredness.
The helm throbs when violence is near, filling the wearer with a compulsion to act.
The water in this cup splashes wildly, like storm-tossed waves. Although drops slosh over the lid every few seconds, the cup never seems to empty.
Stained by blood, and gifted to only the most faithful of True Souls to help preserve their lives.
The dull shine of the adamantine promises this shield could take a thousand beatings - and still look as good as new.
Embroidered with a simple maxim - 'Nature is the True State of the World' - these hides radiate a faint divine power.
Two lice still scurry around on the little flap of skin attached to this clump of matted, crusty hair.
Data.TechnicalDescription: Consuming this piece of fey flesh grants a permanent +1 bonus to <LSTag Tooltip="Intelligence">Intelligence</LSTag>.

Data.Description: A gossamer petal, all that remains of a sussur bloom when drained of its energy or exposed to surface air.
Infused with the inconceivable might of the formidable BOOOAL!
A soft ball of orange slime. It burns uncomfortably hot in your hand.
Damp has seeped through the planks, all but obliterating inscription. The entire barrel smells faintly acrid.
Countless hands have smoothened the haft and sharpened the blade. This is an ancestral weapon - perhaps dating back to the ancient digs that sundered the duergar from their dwarf-kin.
A hymn to Eilistraee is inscribed along the inside of this ring, which is surprisingly heavy when worn.

When the inventor Yrre met the cleric Lenore, sparks flew. Apart, they were in a rut, but together, they inspired each other to push the boundaries of innovation and invention. This ring is just one of their many scientific triumphs.
Tiny bells are sewn into the boots' cuffs. They jingle subtly with every step.
Intricately detailed, down to the tiniest wrinkle on the palm.

Darker than a starless night, Night Walkers are made for secrecy in the honour of Shar.
This particular pair was found deep in the ruins of an Underdark fortress. Though the leather is old and the magic is fading, the boots were recently cleaned and oiled with care.
Clumps of hair and flesh stick out from the twisted roots that make up the shaft of this wand. 'Connor' is scratched into the surface.
More club than scourge, this weapon has a serrated edge made for drawing long, shallow cuts.
It's really very heavy.
Once part of the Girdle of Blades, this buckle was torn off and fashioned into an amulet that can be worn by creatures of all sizes.
A fruity wine with hints of currant and cherry, made with surface-picked grapes and barrel-aged in the dark tunnels of the Wormwrithings.
Entirely inconspicuous, save for the circular pattern in which it grew.
This creature's tiny appendages periodically creep out to poke at its surroundings.
Worked carefully into the locket's metal back are the words, 'Never dark again.'
Data.TechnicalDescription: Grants its wearer the ability to cast <LSTag Type="Spell" Tooltip="Target_DancingLights">Dancing Lights</LSTag>.

Data.Description: This bright blue flower, picked from a budding sussur tree, exudes a honey-sweet aroma, which turns foul and eventually fades away if the bloom is exposed to sunlight.
This amulet, engraved with a small waterfall, imparts a feeling of calm serenity when worn.
Each jewel gleams with the energy of the natural elements.
Broader than a pig's, but shorter. They give off a mouth-watering aroma.

Though they only worked together for a short time, it is hard to overstate the influence Lenore the cleric of Mystra had on Yrre the Sparkstruck, who often likened harnessing lightning to manipulating the Weave.
A common ring, simple and unadorned. Though there is a certain heft to it...
Darkness seems to blossom from this ring, heightened by the menacing glare of the Absolute's symbol, though for the Branded this symbol holds the promise of power.
The air around this staff crackles with a cold, frosty wind - a power that has been divided for too long, and is waiting to be released.
These coins grant the Toll Collector protection against attacks, but will be lost if destroyed.
Once the mighty hallmark of BOOOAL's Chosen, now little more than an ordinary blade.
Putting on this hat is somehow enough to lift your spirits.
Beneath the layers of dust covering this necklace, its inlaid gems still give off a blue sparkle - the colour of Mystra's clergy.
When Yrre the Sparkstruck was asked why they'd created a trident twice their size, they simply replied, 'The question is why not?'
Concocted of rare ingredients that hasten the drinker's demise unless mixed correctly.
Data.TechnicalDescription: Nullifies the effects of certain duergar poisons, grants <LSTag Tooltip="Advantage">Advantage</LSTag> on <LSTag Tooltip="SavingThrow">Saving Throws</LSTag> against being Poisoned, and grants <LSTag Tooltip="Resistant">Resistance</LSTag> to Poison damage.

Data.Description: Though heavy, this longsword swings effortlessly in your hand - ready to take down a hundred enemies.
Two lice still scurry around on the little flap of skin attached to this clump of matted, crusty hair.
Data.TechnicalDescription: Consuming this piece of fey flesh grants a permanent +1 bonus to <LSTag Tooltip="Constitution">Constitution</LSTag>.

Data.Description: Blessed by Priestess Gut, these gauntlets provide additional aid to any who bear the Absolute's mark upon their flesh.
You sense the shadows that envelop this drowcraft cowl, eagerly waiting to envelop you and shield you from view.
Mud cakes the tiny letters of an inscription - 'A Cursed Sight Doth Dwell Beneath'.
Data.TechnicalDescription: Equip this ring to increase your <LSTag Tooltip="Perception">Perception Skill</LSTag> by [1].

Data.Description: Pulverised minerals and gemstones, mined and traded by the dwarves of Mirabar, give this bowl its bright glaze.
These coins grant the Toll Collector protection against attacks, but will be lost if destroyed.
At the barest touch, you feel a surge of exuberance and stamina - like you could take on anyone and anything.

Crush this gem to charm all creatures around you. When the spell ends, the gemstone fragments will crumble to dust.

Clouds swirl in this stormy grey stone. Now and again, it reflects the sun like a lightning bolt.
Though dust has settled into every nook and cranny of this staff, it still emanates a soothing aura. Its previous owner cast it aside - forgotten because there was nobody to bless.
A shiver of magic flows from this bow into your hand - like a promise.
A waft of sulphur emanates from these proudly-kept gauntlets.
Gamey and succulent. Whoever this belonged to, they led an active life.
Two lice still scurry around on the little flap of skin attached to this clump of matted, crusty hair.
Data.TechnicalDescription: Consuming this piece of fey flesh grants a permanent +1 bonus to <LSTag Tooltip="Wisdom">Wisdom</LSTag>.

Data.Description: These coins grant the Toll Collector protection against attacks, but will be lost if destroyed.
A nimble mace, heavy with the promise of broken bones.
A blade of flawless craft. As it parts the air, you fancy you can hear a faint, whispering shriek...
Plain leather with a faint but unmistakable buzz - as if eager to put idle hands to work.
A soft ball of green slime. Thick drops slide down your fingers, stinging your skin.
A dye created by Imperial Dyemaster Sigurd and his apprentice, Aurora, for those who wish to stride valiantly into a world rife with adventure.
Stained brown and reeking of iron, this greataxe once belonged to a killer so deranged, his name was magically scrubbed from all histories.
Scored with slime and blood, it seems this chain mail shirt couldn't save its previous owner. Although it may help the next.
The gems and pearls of this necklace have a brilliant shine to them, as if reflecting unseen moonlight.
Blowing this horn produces a reverberating, threatening wail.
The ring's arcane jewel parts all but the darkest of shadows.
The adamantine plates lock and slide together perfectly - offering protection against even the deadliest of blades.
A piece of tough bark from a sussur tree. Holding it leaves a dull tingling in your fingers.
When the light hits it just so, the centre jewel shimmers with every colour of the rainbow.
The runes encircling this ring appear to have been scratched into the metal with a rock.
These coins grant the Toll Collector protection against attacks, but will be lost if destroyed.
Two lice still scurry around on the little flap of skin attached to this clump of matted, crusty hair.
Data.TechnicalDescription: Consuming this piece of fey flesh grants a permanent +1 bonus to <LSTag Tooltip="Charisma">Charisma</LSTag>.

Data.Description: These pants, cinched at the waist, are stained with splotches of brown and crimson.
The Dwarven grammar is garbled, but the weapon's name suggests something about the importance of first impressions.
A strong sulphurous smell emanates from this magical machine.
This ring coaxes anyone branded by the Absolute. Their fingers veritably itch to slip it on.
Drips unpleasantly when squeezed.
Don't be fooled - this 'potion' will leave you worse for wear.
Yrre the Sparkstruck was raised in the Underdark, so they weren't surprised that power begets envy, and envy begets violence. They were prepared.
The smooth, six-pointed star on this ring is beset with small Underdark gemstones, as befits a talisman of the god of mining and patron of deep gnomes.
The leather smells faintly of herbs, as if washed in a herbal bath.

The branches of this circlet are half-fossilised, passed down through generations of druids. Fabricated during the founding of the grove, the wreath is forever linked to its lands, the tiny rubies connected to its stones and structures, bidding them to do their bidding.

Data.DisplayName: Volo's Complete Guide to the Behaviour of Nymphs
Data.Description: The heavily edited draft of a book that examines the activities of nymphs in GREAT detail.
An exotic gossamer petal, faded and blue. It smells faintly of honey.
Rough, unprocessed and raw - this mithral ore is ready to be fed into the forge.
Blackened drops of blood have coagulated on the outside of the bottle and stained its stopper.
This watery sludge slowly drips off your spoon.
Deep and dark, like a starless night.
Fashioned together from a rough-cut branch and stinking sinew.
Entirely inconspicuous, save for the circular pattern in which it grew.
A simple horn belonging to Lump the Enlightened. The mouthpiece is crusty with chunks of dried food.
Data.TechnicalDescription: Sound this horn to call Lump's frenzied band of ogres. They will feast on anyone they can get their hands on, but if you've made a deal with them, they will make an effort to spare your party.

Data.DisplayName: U. R. : For the Absolute's Glory
Data.Description: Grand Duke Ravengard's personal reflections.
Somewhere deep in the spongy grey matter and little jiggly bits that comprise the brain, the memory of the slimy tadpole slithering over your eyeball lingers...
Created by a warmongering rakshasa and kept for a time under the careful watch of an astute noble named Lord de'Arnise, this flail is a tool of absolute destruction, and a versatile one at that.

Data.DisplayName: The Most Holy Sermons of Lashbearer Catrine

Data.Description: A simple, plain tome detailing the daily routines and meditations of a monastic novice.
Snatched from the realm of the mad wizard Halaster Blackcloak, this knife became a prized keepsake of a duergar king.
A gnomish captive makes an offer to his captor.
A brief survival guide for new Flaming Fist recruits.
Sheet music for a martial bardic tune.
One of Blood Vendor Araj Obladra's elixirs, distilled from a specific sanguine quality, and with properties aligned to an equally specific race.
Data.TechnicalDescription: Mundane pluckiness grants you <LSTag Tooltip="Proficiency">Proficiency</LSTag> in all <LSTag Tooltip="Skill">skills</LSTag> until the next <LSTag Tooltip="LongRest">Long Rest</LSTag> due to the wily resourcefulness now bubbling within it.

Data.Description: A hand-written note, mysterious in its intention
The soles of these boots warp and shift like warm clay manipulated by an unseen sculptor's hands.
Magic weapon meant to slay a particular kind of creature, sparrows in this case. The arrow will grievously wound sparrows it hits, the poor wee winged fellows.

One of the relics of Deep Duerra's rebellious children. Paranoid by nature, Duerra had erected a vast array of biting, blasting, blinding traps and safeguards to keep her enemies from gaining her sanctum.

Of course, this also meant her children were sealed in with her by those same deadly measures.
A gracefully rendered bard dances within this portrait's frame. The artist has captured something unique in her eyes - almost as if more than one soul sits behind them.

Cradling his newborn son awkwardly, the Duke's face pulled into a rictus of misery. His love Francesca smiled at him, briefly, and died. He stared at her until the boy cried, and he told the boy it would be all right, though he himself did not believe it.

Data.DisplayName: Reflections Upon the Mirror of Loss
Magical Histories, Volume 3: The Second Sundering

Data.Description: Selûnite Brooch embossed with 'A + I'

Data.DisplayName: Report on Activities of Enver Gortash
Urgent - Rapid Increase in Reported Disapperances

Data.Description: This petite flute, engraved with drow sigils, is said to have belonged to Captain Dostrealt of the spelljammer flitter 'Erevan's Clutch'.

Mantled in the sublime majesty of this cloak, you magically sense Lorroakan's complex feelings for his homeland. Merriment and comfort go hand in hand with a jilted sentiment around his lovers and his family. And the old friends he thought of, but would never see again.

Fragments of dead souls are imprisoned in the steel. Angry, powerful, hopeful, or scared - all of them rose up against their illithid masters, and all of them fell to this blade. Now, they are trapped forever, forced to aid their oppressors.
A note found on the corpse of a woman underneath the Open Hand Temple.
A heartfelt letter from a faraway kingdom.
Formerly wielded by one who forsook all ties of friendship and kindness, this sword is rife with deranged energies. It seems to transmit feelings of contentment when carving through bones.
The holder of this pass is permitted entry to the city of Baldur's Gate. The pass bears the waxen seal of Investigator Valeria.
Acid was long ago abandoned by assassins, who found poison much more reliable in spiking their targets' drinks. The acid kept melting the chalices.
A note found on the corpse of a tall man in the Lower City.

This helm, worn atop the pate of Balduran the Brave, still gleams as if with the untarnished splendour of his legacy. Baldur's Gate itself bears his name, and tales of his exploits have turned the heads and hearts of many.
