The lip of the pack is stitched with the likeness of a helmeted warrior, their eyes sheltered. Something protrudes from the helm, like a strange, floppy arrow.

Data.DisplayName: From the Desk of Enver Gortash
Scorching Street - A Flaming Fist Ruleset

Data.Description:
Monster-slaying is a rare calling, not for the faint of heart. It requires temperance, discipline, and usually a very big stick with something pointy at the end.
The best thing about spears is that the ugly parts of combat are happening at the other end.
The dagger's twisting blade is designed to nick the flesh as many times as possible, allowing its paralytic poison to flow effortlessly into any unfortunate target.
Stitched into the lining is the phrase: 'Yes all right, all right, stop moaning and get up.'
A dagger that thrums with desire - a longing for vengeance.

Data.DisplayName: Orpheus, Prince of the Comet, Part One: Betrayal
Data.Description: A round slate with circular symbols etched into it.
Crowded taprooms. Packed feast halls. Bustling market bazaars. Chances to be social? Sure. Chances to be violent? Absolutely.
A 'Crazy Wilbur' is a technique invented by the dwarvish Ticklebeard Clan. It involves getting your larger enemies to swallow your weapon, then calling it back to you - as messily as possible.

The platinum inlays of this halberd hum an otherworldly harmony in the key of C, heightening the wielder's vigour but diminishing their mental faculties. The sound it makes is pining, as if far from its rightful home.

Data.DisplayName: Servitor of the Black Hand Gloves
Data.Description: Covetous of Mystra's command of the Weave, Bane the Black Hand extends his grasp, each finger comprised of ten thousand fanatics, adjuncts of his evil will.
This ornately decorated bell, tarnished with age, rings with a mischevious giggle not unlike its pixie enchanter.

To break one's oath is a dangerous game - it marks you as a faithless cur, an exile without a cause. This armour is tempered by an age of rocks, blades, and persecution turned against it - and is buffed by the immutable, unbindable will of its wearer.
This quarterstaff is as solid as the bond between each member of the Harpers - even working in anonymity, they do so with a common and righteous cause.
A potion brewed by the merregons to charm a displacer beast. This batch seems weaker and might only addle the mind.
Rogues in Waterdeep prefer these spring-loaded boots that make evading the city watch a breeze.

Data.DisplayName: The Apprentice's Companion, Book the Fourth

Data.Description: All the bang and the boom of the original, but with an extra surprise.
When Gandrel was seven, he was frightened badly by a vampire spawn during a public burning. Seized by the flames, the creature didn't shrivel up. It swelled and burst.
The air around this armour shimmers, oven-hot. From the seams of the armour you can hear a red-tinted rumble, like coals digesting in a furnace.
They say rich folk are never truly happy: especially true when they're targeted with this morningstar.
Many a githyanki hunter has worn this amulet before you. The strange stones set in swirling silver reverberate with echoes of their magic.
The commonly held belief that archers are rangey, thin-wristed people is completely false. It takes years of training to pull a bowstring all the way back to your cheekbone, and wrists like iron.
Elegant motifs of warding - shields, targes, bucklers, and buffers - are faintly impressed into the metal round of the ring.

Data.DisplayName: The Apprentice's Companion, Book the First

Data.Description: The last sight Sarevok witnessed as a mortal was his sibling's knife. This duel, the first between Bhaalspawn, is worshipped still by the cult of Bhaal, who now believe that no act is more sacred than fratricide between spawn before the altar of their Dread Lord.
Traversing fast-paced bodies of water is a chore for all - apart from the fashionable folk clad in this footwear.
A brusque-looking dwarf is picked out in broad, evocative brushstrokes. His magnificent hat is bettered only by his beard.
A new invention of the Sharess' Caress bartender Hoots - like being decked in the sobriety.
The snakefolk of Chult are not known for waste, so often forge lightweight and robust armour like this from their own shed skin.
Bands of blue light snap and contract when the gloved fingertips are pressed together - evidence of the arcane polarity linking them.
An advisory text suggesting that when powerful forces attack, union is the most appropriate goal.
An old issue of the Baldur's Mouth Gazette.
When light catches this ring at the right angle, it pulses with a dizzying, intoxicating glow befitting the jewellery of the Prince of the Comet.

One of the relics of Deep Duerra's rebellious children. Drugging the Keykeeper of Duerra's vaults, the children crept in under cover of night and plundered their mother's treasure - searching desperately for anything that would aid in their flight.

Data.DisplayName: Music and Lyrics: 'The Queen's High Seas'
Data.Description: Sheet music for a rousing bardic tune.
Built for function rather than fun.

A variant of this halberd's design was thrown out in the early stages of development by its forgemaster. This was because the halberd kept expressing itself. 'ALARM!' it would shriek in peril. 'POTENCY FILLS ME LIKE A SONG OF HOPE!' it roared in triumph.

Data.DisplayName: Magical Histories, Volume 4: The Chosen of Mystra

Data.Description: When not atop their dragons, gith are not particularly air-worthy. This is probably for the best. The imposition of downward gravity tends to put most people in a mood.

Data.DisplayName: To the Best of Wives and Mothers
Data.Description: A tarnished ring engraved with the following: 'To Ffion, Best of Wives and Best of Mothers.'
Long may these gird the Blade of Frontiers.
Supposedly fashioned around a lock of hair stolen from the head of the Prince of Gloomwrought, shields of this ilk gladly welcome the dark.

Not the most elegant of weapons, the warpick's cumbersome weight certainly allows it to be deadly in combat, when wielded by a strong arm. Inexplicably, this one has a small rabbit carved into the handle.
Otto, a member of the powerful arcane organisation the Circle of Eight, had a penchant for amulets. So much so that they announced his arrival before he ever needed to.

What was life like before the mind flayers snatched you up? Road dust clots your boots, campfires roar up and diminish, faces swim by.

More and more that life distances itself like some other world. A dream world maybe, glimpsed now and again through a gauze.
It is said that Carixim, the fiendish titan whose flesh squirms with twenty-thousand trapped souls, forged the pieces of this armour set.

A garment worn by one of three monks who fought together against Headless Serpent, Secret Venom, a gang in the port city of Nyanzaru. This was worn by Strigga Morkoscavich, whose stances moved fluidly, flawlessly, and who defanged the Serpent one blustery night.

Data.DisplayName: To Oliver Tefoco, The Bee Hive, Stormshore Street, Baldur's Gate

Data.Description:
During a hilltop battle that soaked the slopes in gore, Kushigo's best friend Irishi was scalped before he could help her.

The enemy held up the bloody wig, and Kushigo fell upon one, and then another, until he had killed so many that they hung from his antlered shoulders like skewered effigies.
A gnomish adventurer once used this to outpace his enemies down a slope.

Data.DisplayName: Adventures on the Sea of Fallen Stars

Data.Description: The top of this skull is cracked with a lattice of shallow fractures.
Huntresses prowling in the least hospitable woods of Toril hold one rule as cardinal: kill quickly. This is not about suffering. It's about sound, and its necessary absence.
This robe is a difficult look to pull off unless one is blessed with an otherworldly charisma.

In spite of (or perhaps because of) his suspiciously amusing name, the wizard Melf was actually quite a talented spellcaster and innovator in the field of the arcane. He even led an order called the Knights of Luna.
This robe once belonged to one of the great wizard Tenser's lecturers. While in university, Tenser used to practise spells on this robe, sometimes resulting in wonderful arcane discovery.

This hammer's weight is centred on enchanted obsidian at the base of the head. Some nights before bed, Ketheric would sneak a whey-faced glance at the hammer, and think about the stone, and wonder what unknown facet of his heart bore his weight.
Quivers creep up your enemy's back - the slow, long-fingered hand of your magic.

Glutted with lone wolves and well-meaning scallywags, the Harpers are not averse to shadows - quite the contrary. For many such individuals, being swallowed in the dark throat of the night is the only method they know, or care to know.
The notorious gnomish bard Fiddlesticks Glimmergad was said to play violin tunes so sad they made bank guards weep - while his accomplices robbed the bank's vaults.
The air surrounding this lavishly decorated amulet is thick - like pushing your fingers through sap or syrup.
Heavy and grouted in the gore of countless centuries, this prototype for the contemporary githyanki silver sword was wielded during their rebellion against the mind flayers who enslaved them.
A small iron key.
A makeshift grenade that unleashes a storm of scrap metal upon detonation.

One of the relics of Deep Duerra's rebellious children. It was to the tremendous surprise of all that Ludmilla, the quiet, the weepy, the daughter most under her mother's thumb, took up this bow and fired.

The arrow flashed, and while Duerra and her blinded court wailed impotently, the children escaped into an uncertain, yet sweetly free, future.
This gemstone used to be in a ring.

Data.DisplayName: A key that unlocks the display case in the House of Hope Archive.

Data.Description: Named after Harold Butterbisk, who owned the Butterbisk Inn in Waterdeep before it was renamed by new owners. The stock of the crossbow reads: Quaffing is a shootable offence.
Odd to think that dark gods like Bhaal were once mortal. One wonders if they ever thumbed a wagon ride, thought about the weather, or ate flavoured yoghurt.
Linked to her with fell magic, these mushrooms keep Auntie Ethel alive until they are destroyed.
A gift from Dame Aylin and her radiant goddess, this weapon's contours hold a silver-white beauty akin to the nightly lantern that climbs the firmament each evening.
Dark smoke swirls in the ring's onyx, protecting something within.
This key can open any room in Sharess' Caress.
The fur is so blue as to be almost black. When mantled across your shoulders, the patterns on the cloak seem to shift and ripple.
The ring from the djinni who worked in the circus. Its magic certainly explains how the djinni was able to cheat at the wheel.
When the archer Frederik Durlusk died, his only request was to be buried with his favourite bow. This is that bow.
Strong castle-forged steel surmounts a grip of sturdy leather - this immense sword is capable of disembowelling giants in a single swipe.
Simmering in the heartwood of this staff, you sense a latent power pulsating - it seems the thing is impatient to build up and dispense its fierce energy.

This was created by a designer and an enchanter who were going through a messy divorce at the time. As such, the armour is filled with active-aggressive rage. It also makes you feel like you've wasted the last ten years picking up after a complete tit.

Data.TechnicalDescription: Summons Balthazar's Flesh Golem during combat. This item is only functional in the Gauntlet of Shar.

Data.DisplayName: Gond and Gripping Life By The Tongs

Data.Description: Fingering this amulet sends a spike of pleasure sliding through the brain - pleasure that could be turned to pain in an enemy's addled mind.
A small iron key.
One of Blood Vendor Araj Obladra's elixirs, distilled from a specific sanguine quality, and with properties aligned to an equally specific race.
Data.TechnicalDescription: Upon consumption, you and surrounding allies regain <LSTag Tooltip="HitPoints">hit points</LSTag> equal to your Constitution <LSTag Tooltip="Abilities">score</LSTag>.

Data.Description: Barely-perceptible magic flows from this unusual device. It is searching, seeking, listening...

Folded into the steel of this menacing weapon is an alloy of enchanted metal. It waits like a leech in thick swamp water, awaiting a victim to taste, awaiting a chance to restore your heartiness and inflict suffering on your foes.
'When I found Carixim, he turned to me, with all those poor people's souls crammed into him, and he... he grinned at me. He said, "I been expecting you, boy."' - Overheard from the smith Dammon
Clever enchantments dance between the grooves of this shield, which emanates a magic of heightened awareness.

'You drop and give me thirty you sumbitch; you think a bugbear's gonna roll over and let you rub his tummy? One two three four - keep going maggot! Stronger, better, tougher!' - Any Sword Coast Drill Sergeant, Invariably
A plain, unadorned note.
The point of the rapier is capable of splitting into heated barbs, should the wielder decide to prick themselves to activate them - sacrifice for reward.
A receipt of ownership stipulating cost and binding change of ownership.
Excruciatingly precise lines bring this portrait's undead subject to life. Despite his empty eye sockets, you could almost swear his gaze follows you - judgementally.
A limp scrap of parchment marked by a childish hand.
Though the ring is highly polished, darkened slivers of blood still cling to small scrapes and corners.
The harsh but invigorating coffee in this drink is tempered by a soothing milk tea - best supped in grand plazas of music and blue-pink light.
Tenser's notes on arcane displacement were not only read by wizards - other avid readers included enterprising smiths eager to break into the magic items market.
Magic got caught in this heirloom by being exposed to too many wizard family dinners.
In the palm of the left glove is a glossy scarlet solution that coats Thieves' Tools, making them more reliable. In the right, arcane symbols wax and wane.
Where most people see a bundle of interesting diseases in the common rat, members of the Zhentarim syndicate see a potential colleague.

Data.DisplayName: Fake Portrait of a Noble Before His Death
Data.Description: A counterfeit piece of art.
A catalogue of potions written by Bileous Quimsy, a genius herbologist.
These flexible shoes were once owned by Audreyne Willoughs, who, in a somewhat ironic twist of fate, ran away from the circus to join her parents back home.
Light as thoughts themselves, this dagger is in the habit of rending them, causing significant pain, and occasional death.
Though the leather is slick with acid, the corrosive liquid doesn't seem to damage the boots - nor does it penetrate.

Data.DisplayName: Manual of Hilaritie for the Trulie Unfunnie

Data.Description: Adorned in a fanned coronet of speartip points, its mask fixed with stiff-lipped intent, this helmet evokes a frightful, almost alien aspect that gestures to Shar. For she is strange and terrible indeed.
This exquisite instrument is said to come from the shop of the legendary Moonshaean bard Falataer. Fewer than twenty of his handcrafted lyres still survive.
Salvaged from the beard of a dead infernal leviathan, whose facial hair was formed from the weapons of an army it had once vanquished.
A metal key held by a tiefling refugee. A notch has been carved in the handle.
An old lute that hums with the voices of numerous sprites and spirits.

The shield is so battered, its metallic portions have the look of a creased grey shirt. However, underneath those folds of steel, scintillas of arcane light glimmer, echoing the hidden power of the Enforcers.

Data.DisplayName: Invasion Plans for the Sword Coast
Data.Description: A plain, unadorned note.

Data.DisplayName: Veronica Hamperclips and her Adventures Beyond The Washbasin
Her Love For It Was Like A Plum
Night of the Red Moon: Valarken's Coup

Data.Description: This delicate circlet grants its wearer the ability to cast the Scorching Ray spell.
Peals of thunder rumble at the back of your skull with every step taken in these boots.
The weight of the interwoven steel rings is offset by clever elven craftsmanship - rustling against your undershirt, the mail feels like you're wearing a cloud.

Data.DisplayName: The Butler's Cane Has A Knob On The End

Data.Description: Whenever the wearer steals anything, a piece of coal appears in their pocket, like a tiny, dusty condemnation.
Created by a designer and an enchanter who were going through a messy divorce at the time. As such the armour is filled with passive-aggressive rage.
When asked how he felt about weapons that return to you when thrown, famous adventurer Lupperdiddle Swires responded, 'Not for me. They remind me too much of someone I used to know.'
Data.TechnicalDescription: This shield <LSTag Type="Status" Tooltip="WEAPON_BOND">Binds</LSTag> to your being, returning to your hand if thrown.

Data.Description: An article block primed for loading into an eager printing press.
This unusually shaped crest bears the markings of a Lathanderian high priest, but its practical function is unclear.
Floral needles of scent thread the air around this extract with the smell of honeysuckle, balmy eucalyptus, crocus and cyclamen.

A memory from her childhood: a warm bed. Through the cracked window, she could see the moonlight cupping the plums in the tree as if in silver hands. The name of the goddess Selûne came to her, and never left.

The wizard Otiluke wrote about bound weapons and their propensity to coalesce with their wielder as the pair come together. He also wrote about their dangers, which are manifold, and their benefits, which make the danger worth it.
Data.TechnicalDescription: This blade's magical powers only function if it's <LSTag Type="Status" Tooltip="WEAPON_BOND">Bound</LSTag> to an Eldritch Knight or is a Warlock's <LSTag Type="Status" Tooltip="PACT_BLADE">Pact Weapon</LSTag>.

Data.Description: Provocative light blooms from the engraved contours of this ring.
Quiet is the air around this sword, and quiet are the steps of the one who wields it.
Data.TechnicalDescription: Shortsword of Stealth

Data.Description:
One of the relics of Deep Duerra's rebellious children.

Kitted out though they were for escape, the older siblings had a horrible time encouraging their younger brothers and sisters, who at the crux were frightened of what their mother would do to them should they be caught.
A pair of pixie wings were used to create this pretty blade - their delicate tracings can be seen all day and night, though they shine brightest by the light of a gibbous moon.
The previous owner was going to call this sword Barney, but he got such a bollocking from his friends that he named it Fleshrender instead, and sulked for a whole tenday afterward.

Forsaking his infamous armour, Kushigo left Irishi's body and wandered naked, without thought or care, into the barren countryside. The land was flat and desolate under the red-gold sun, but compared to his lonely heart, it seemed alive with joy.
Sheet music for an earnest bardic tune.
With the forest's illusion dispelled, this apple's lethal nature has become readily apparent.

Data.DisplayName: SOUPS OF THE REALMS BY BROTHER DONNICK

Data.Description: Once there was a man who dreamed of unlocking every bit of his potential. It upset him when he couldn't; after all who can? When his daughter was born, she taught him about real dreams. She taught him with her eyes.
Fizzling barbs of enchantment magic crackle from the laces of these boots.

Data.DisplayName: For the Eyes Of Lady Jannath ONLY

Data.Description: The slogan "Holy Hand Soap - for washing yer hands of dirt, muck, 'n even blasphemy!" adorns this rudimentary bottle.

Layered sheets of smelted, shaped, and smithed steel have been etched with a sweetly luminous gold. Its outward appearance is heavy. And yet it's so light when you lift it, like lifting a bag of shrunken dead leaves.
An elaborate key, plated with silver.

Bhaal, Lord of Murder, was forced to walk the world as a mortal man during a period of history called the Time of Troubles. He was more vulnerable than he had ever been.

But Bhaal was cunning. He had contingencies in case he died.
An elaborate key, plated with silver.
A perfect system must be ruled by a keen eye - and any error foolish enough to rear its head afore the eye must be quickly, precisely, and totally eliminated. This crossbow can help with that.
Adjusting this unassuming ring on your finger, you hear a faint sizzle, as of pressure being released.
After the blade had sliced Kas the Bloody-Handed's throat, it was chosen by Pelor, God of the sun, to do righteous work against the undead.

Data.DisplayName: Note About the Shield of Silvam

Data.Description: Carved in circles across the knob of the staff are different words for thunder. Gnomish, Sylvan, Elvish, Celestial, even the Primordial tongue - all of these and more fuse together to form the thunderword.
An egg-like shell of spiny bones and rotting feathers. Necromantic energy oozes from within.
When active, teleports whoever who touches it to a new location.
You can cast <LSTag Type="Spell" Tooltip="Target_MistyStep">Misty Step</LSTag>, with the caveat that you will teleport leaving your clothes behind.

A garment worn by one of three monks who fought together against Headless Serpent, Secret Venom, a gang in the port city of Nyanzaru. This was worn by Kimigha Poji, whose stances were narrow and swift.
This powerful tome radiates energy that settles in your chest, threatening to pull tears from a place you never knew.
Every adventuring party has at least one 'chaotic element'. In the case of one such party, this was the infamous Scabby, a barbarous goblin who was trained by monks.
Tight, aerodynamic, and built for maximum breathability. Humidity is no friend to hamsters.
Rudimentary teleportation sigils mark the palms of these gloves, like coiled snakes in a bath of pitch.
Imbued with a little luck after the item was pressed to the pursed lips of a saint of the goddess Tymora.
While the leather is clean and well-maintained, a cold, acrid smell permeates these gloves.
Organisations like the Harpers do not relegate their activities to head-to-head combat - many a moonlit chase with an evildoer has been resolved with a loose roof tile and a decent throwing arm.

These gloves were worn by the wizard Bucknard, who always maintained that speed was most important in spellcasting. This, because even if you royally bugger up the spell, you've got enough time to leg it away afterward.
Embroidered into the cloth: 'If you're reading this, you managed to bed or behead me. Either way, you got lucky.'
Fell magic has seeped into this circlet, rejoicing at the slightest touch of despair.

Data.DisplayName: Boom, Bang, Blast: The joy of fireworks
Data.Description: An illustrated guide to the creation of explosives penned by the proprieter of Felogyr's Fireworks.

One of the relics of Deep Duerra's rebellious children. The children found nothing of use in the vault and were discouraged.

But in the morning the Vault Keykeeper's son, who admired the children, sought them out - and in his arms he brought a wealth of things, forged in shadow.
The planar silver cladding of these forearm bracers allows the wielder to channel the latent astral energies floating in the Weave.

Coming upon a wise woman, Kushigo got drunk and grew maudlin, and told her about Irishi's scalping. She gave him some clothes - light and fine - and encouraged him to take his time to grieve. He did.

And, when he was ready, he fought again, uninhibited by steel or fellowship - for they only weighed him down.
This battered order of service bears the wear of many hands opening it.
A cornered animal will, on occasion, feel a rush of exhilarating energy, and an urge to fight. The same is true of many arcane practitioners, who do not take kindly to being menaced.
This messily annotated scrap of parchment emits a dreadful stench.
'Walking Fortress' is a defensive technique reliant on a shield of this caliber. It involves upsetting your opponent who just wants to land a single blow.

Data.DisplayName: Codicilliary Rules of Engagements for the Flaming Fist

Data.Description: A small iron key.
The heart of the gem seems to flow like liquid - yet it contains neither quicksilver nor mercury.

When Allandra was a girl, she saw a hot spall of matter fire through the sky. She wished upon this falling star, but instead of getting an answer from the sky, she got one from the sea in the voice of Umberlee, goddess of the endless fathom.
Clownish clothes adorn this dead sack of unanimated flesh. There's a little flower that squirts water.
Energy crackles in weird and wonderful patterns across your hand as you wield this bound weapon, as if your very veins were marbled like a cloud of blue-white lightning.
Data.TechnicalDescription: This hammer's magical powers only function if it's <LSTag Type="Status" Tooltip="WEAPON_BOND">Bound</LSTag> to an Eldritch Knight or is a Warlock's <LSTag Type="Status" Tooltip="PACT_BLADE">Pact Weapon</LSTag>.

Data.DisplayName: Ethical Review of the Flaming Fist

Data.Description: Delicate ferns of frost glitter in the lining of this robe.
Entirely inconspicuous, save for the circular pattern in which it grew.
A small iron key from the circus beast cage.

The texture of magic granted by a warlock's patron is largely dependent upon the patron themselves - for example, your standard eldritch patron's probably going to work some eyeball-mottled tentacles in there somewhere.
This is a self published book of poetry. It's extremely horny.
Little leech motifs adorn the pad of each finger. The leeches have rows of suckling, sharp teeth.
The sharp metal whispers to you. Pleading. Cursing... Echoes of slain foes.
The bauble is emblazoned with fiendish words that, when translated, mean, 'May your throat be educated in new screams.'

Data.DisplayName: The Watch and the Steel Watch

Data.Description: This stone disc is carved with circular runes and pictographs.
This impaling pole of enchanted steel was commissioned as part of a set by Strahd von Zarovich, who presented the weapons to his honour guard one cold morning.
Unsheathed, the steel of this rapier shivers and thrums mellifluously in response to nearby surfaces - the motion brings to mind an actor struck with pre-show nerves.

Data.DisplayName: Behold Protection's Future: The Steel Watch!

Data.Description: Sheet music for a rollicking bardic tune.
The Absolute's power radiates from this shield, invisible waves of energy beckoning to the Branded.
This letter, penned on official Flaming Fist parchment, is set for the next barracks correspondence dispatch.
Indents on the fingertips of these gloves are ringed with tiny meteorites, lined in a shimmering purple light rather than the rich red of astral flame.
The sun crystal is cut imperfectly. It is still worth a pretty penny, but it's not perfectly symmetrical.
The power of this axe lies in a fluctuating arcane enchantment that flows between the beard and the edge of the axe, and the wielder themselves.

Wielded by Svartlebee The Custodian, so named because he had the following reputation: Have you got someone in your life causing a mess? Send Svartlebee a missive. He shall clean them up, and then clean up the crime scene.
The power of this item lies in belief, though not in any god. This item believes that it's very good at hitting things, so it is. Belief is quite powerful when it comes to violence.
Tinkling, ringing, jangling, and about as festive as a terminal diagnosis.

Earnest little Edith Cluckle was a small girl when she asked to be the great wizard Otiluke's apprentice. He scoffed at her, but was quickly abashed when Mystra herself endowed Edith with this very cloak.
This painting is awash with bold scarlet hues depicting a noble lizard. His snout is raised in a snooty, imperious glare.
Deceptively light, the blade rasps through castle-forged plate as easily as Corellon Larethian's own anarchic holy sword through the hearts of evil orcs.
A note found on the corpse of a blue dragon born in the Lower City.
Decorated with a hummingbird wrought of jade and sapphire, this ring evokes the sheer wonderful quickness of that animal.
Droplets of blood bead the edge of this axe like rain on glass, yet they never drip, and touching them reveals them to be smooth, hard gemstones.

Data.DisplayName: A History of the Flaming Fist
House of Hope - West Wing Key
Data.Description: A small iron key.

When she was a girl, she toyed with nastiness and sadism. Children often grow out of this; they get hobbies. For Orin, that taste for cruelty fermented, and in a way she did find hobbies. Ones that screamed.

The first Dwarven Thrower was created unintentionally. The moment was transcribed in the annals of dwarfdom thusly: 'Ach, it doesn't work. Another design down the bloody drain. Now to... Does er... Does anyone else hear a sort of humming whistle? Growing louder?'
This heavy, deep-voiced instrument is of the type called a 'table lute' due to its weight. Famously, the late Ahndri Stolyarof refused to let anyone else play it.
Often mistaken for a relic of the wizard Bigby's creation, this staff was, ironically, made as a bite stick for Bigby's dog, Bigboy.
Apparently this is what happens to your handwear when you clock an angel in the chops.
Useful for bank vaults, locked chests, and bolted barns.
'Keep your enemies close, and those you want to slit up closer.' - Popular nursery saying
A plain, unadorned note.
This stone disc is carved with circular runes and pictographs.
Brief halos of divine light wrap your head when you don and doff this helmet.
The curve of this sickle evokes a pitiless crescent moon over turbulent seas.
What better way to disguise one's transgressions than a quickly positioned phantasm after the deed is done?
All you need now is a holster for your wand, tobacco to chew, and some sort of pack animal to ride, and you'll look like a complete and utter bingus.
When you slip this ring on your hand and flex your fingers, a boom of discontented thunder grumbles in the air around you.
It might be your imagination, but when blood runs over the blade, you could swear you hear... slurping.

A year into their union, Lenore, cleric of Mystra, gifted the gnome inventor Yrre an invention of her own devising - a ring that held a spell of sparks. Eventually, the touch of Lenore's hand faded to a glinting memory, but the ring's tingling grip remained resolute.

Fused in a macabre and powerful union, three netherstones reflect the triarchy of the Dead Three: Myrkul, Bhaal, and Bane. As in geometrics, the triangular shape proves more stable than any linear or other structure, and the wearer of this crown feels - exquisite and tenebrous - the will to dominate flowing through them.
Data.TechnicalDescription: With all three stones combined, you can now cast <LSTag Type="Spell" Tooltip="Target_END_Mindflayer_CrownDomination">Karsus' Compulsion</LSTag>.

Data.Description: Fell magic has seeped into this circlet, rejoicing at the slightest touch of despair.
Energy crackles around these. Gale wouldn't... Surely he didn't enchant his...
A symbol of a proud stag is burned into the side of this crate.
The magic of this mask comes from its gory provenance, and makes it perfect for the discerning actor, sleuth, or person with a mirror and time to kill.

Data.DisplayName: Recipe of Elixir of Necrotic Resistance

Data.Description: A makeshift spear fashioned from a giant crab's claw and the charged imagination of kuo-toa fishfolk.
One of Blood Vendor Araj Obladra's elixirs, distilled from a specific sanguine quality, and with properties aligned to an equally specific race.
Data.TechnicalDescription: You have <LSTag Tooltip="Advantage">Advantage</LSTag> on Intimidation and Persuasion <LSTag Tooltip="AbilityCheck">Checks</LSTag>, <LSTag Tooltip="Resistant">Resistance</LSTag> to Cold damage, and can use <LSTag Type="Spell" Tooltip="Target_MOO_BloodPotion_IceStorm">Ice Storm</LSTag> once until your next <LSTag Tooltip="LongRest">Long Rest</LSTag>.

Data.Description: Each ring and clash of this sword is a dark melody from the last mortal orchestra in Elysium, Avernus, or both.

Data.DisplayName:
Populism and Propaganda
Stack of paper

Data.Description: Apostle diary in Moonrise, found in Ketheric's room.
Worn by Lumi, a cleric beholden to twilight, who sheltered her fellow adventurers as a bantam shelters her chicks.
A dog-eared copy of the Baldur's Mouth Gazette.

Data.DisplayName: Music and Lyrics: 'Of Divinity and Sin'
Data.Description: Sheet music for a sweeping bardic tune.

Wizards Otiluke and Bigby may be renowned as dignified members of the Circle of Eight, but on one occasion, as younger men, Bigby bet Otiluke that he couldn't suck thirteen litres of vodka out of a protection cloak like this one.

Bigby won.

The charmers, seducers, philanderers, flirts, gallants, beguilers, ravishers, rogues, tempters, and tantalisers of the Feywild all share one common trait: they make you feel as if you are the only diamond among the drift.
Faint whispers creep from this Sending Shell when you hold it close, yet the method of sending messages from it is unclear.
The corner of modern fashion that this hat currently occupies might well be called Optimistic.
The sheer mortal terror of the low-vitality spellcaster (who can be blown over by a wafted spoon) can be partially offset by cloaks like this one.

Data.DisplayName: The Pronunciation of Common for Monstrous Species: A Guide for Pedagogues

Data.Description: Oliver would watch his father split logs with this, enjoying the thwacking sound. Sometimes, in that part of dusk when the light gets thin, he was drawn to his father's shadow, and would feel a stir of inexplicable dread.
The inside of this robe is dark and faceted like volcanic glass, yet the material is light and soft. Against the skin, it also produces a heat like a toasty fire on a day of snow.
Scribbled with inscrutable instructions and lists, this page is written in Lorroakan's elaborate hand.
A shrewd, wily elf is perched in the foreground of this painting, ready to sink her carefully illustrated blades into an unsuspecting target.
A gift from Khalid for Jaheira.
In mellow light, the halberd's curved steel head eerily resembles a grin.

Data.DisplayName: 'An History of the Society of Brilliance as Told by Its Members'

Data.Description: Long ago, Kushigo was a warrior. Bedecked in enormous, stag-antlered plate, his arrival spelled doom for the enemy. This flimsy cloth speaks nothing to that legacy.

Umberlee, the goddess of the sea, is deeply capricious, intelligent, and not nearly as wet around the edges as her domain might suggest. She often demands sacrificial tribute from sailors, such as their ships, their cargo, and, while she's at it, them.
Gazing through this ring, you find that there is no other side, only a small sucking blackness that defies explanation.
For some paladins, the iron-clad grip that an oath holds can be too much to bear. When these champions fail and falter, their hands that would guide turn cold, hard, and piercing.
One of Blood Vendor Araj Obladra's elixirs, distilled from a specific sanguine quality, and with properties aligned to an equally specific race.
Data.TechnicalDescription: You are <LSTag Tooltip="Proficiency">Proficient</LSTag> in Sleight of Hand <LSTag Tooltip="SkillChecks">Checks</LSTag> and can cast <LSTag Type="Spell" Tooltip="Target_Knock">Knock</LSTag> until your next <LSTag Tooltip="LongRest">Long Rest</LSTag> thanks to the crafty wiles of the Forgotten Folk.

Data.Description: Orin's Ring
Concussive energy thumps like a mighty heartbeat from this pike.
A beautiful manuscript made from expensive, high-quality parchment.
It was through scrying and observing blazing elementals that the monks of Plumgully Temple mastered the art of fighting fire with fists, and vice versa.
Bolts slot into this crossbow with wonderful ease, as if eager to nestle against the stock, soon to fly.
Umbral claws sweep through the long slender facets of the blade.
The famous drow with his heart of gold, Drizzt Do'Urden, is not the pioneer of the 'twin sword style' of fighting, though he was among the best practitioners.

The trauma of becoming a drider is quickly set aside with a cold arachnid dispassion. This sword follows that disturbing trend - a replenishing poison gland is built within, deployed only against trapped opponents.
Fashioned from the hard, unforgiving trunk of an oak, this club still retains the perfume of the forest.
An mass-printed tome featuring ornate illustrations of each letter of the alphabet.
'I'm a talented shapeshifter, too. I can shapeshift a thin body into a fat body. All I need is a steady supply of mince pies and mulled wine.' - Overheard in a tavern in Daggerford
Necromantic energy pulses from this dark contraption. It whirrs and hums like a quiet furnace, but feels ice-cold to the touch.

Data.DisplayName: Fake Portrait of a Noble Before His Death
Data.Description: A counterfeit piece of art.

Data.DisplayName: Magical Histories, Volume 1: The Origins of Mystra

Data.Description: Really gives the monks something to pray about, the morning after.
Each blow landed while wearing these gloves produces the rumbling boom of a thousand demons' ravenous stomachs.
Every one of the three gems in this ring is searing hot - enough to burn yourself with the slightest brush of your fingers.

While many drow revere arachnids, there is undoubtedly a degree of emulation at work in the case of certain loathsome sects - look no further than the spiderlike coldness of the Lolthite community for proof of this mimicry.
There are no molluscs of power, alas.
Cracking your knuckles in these gloves dislodges puffy drifts of snow from your fingers.
A plain, unadorned note.

Sages over the course of ages have dealt very constructive and useful advice - however, none so sagacious as that of the wizard Otiluke, who once advised one of his students thusly: 'Never cast Speak with Dead on a loved one if there's unresolved tension there. It's never worth it. Trust me.'
Glibness is not only in the tongue, but in the body. Gesture is powerful. Think of how many words of comfort can be stored and saved, when a hug will do just as sweetly.
A smattering of tiny ice crystals have formed cleats on the soles of these hardy boots.
One of the relics of Deep Duerra's rebellious children. A mean-minded parent, Duerra quickly earned her children's enmity. In secret, the children devised a plan to escape their mother forever.

In the theatre of dreams, Ketheric killed his wife every night. That wasn't how things happened... but always upon waking, he would glare into the dark, long-faced and solemn, and he would think: 'I keep you alive with my memories, beloved. I kill you with what I've become.'
Each sapphire feels like a tiny shard of sharpened ice.

'When I found Carixim, he turned to me, all those poor people's souls crammed into him like too many bees in a rotten hive, and he... He grinned at me. And he said: I been expecting you, boy.' - Overheard from the smith Dammon
A messy map of the city Sewers with a big rather amateurish X drawn on it.

Data.DisplayName: Journal Log of True Soul Korliss

Data.Description: A tyrant's grip must be one of cool, unforgiving, and intricately realised steel. It cannot budge, cannot falter, no matter the pressure, and its fingertips must deeply pierce those who would struggle against it.
Life is just a series of risks taken while blindfolded.

Data.DisplayName: A Home for Every Working Baldurian!

Data.Description: Spectators are hideous aberrations that float above the ground, fiercely staring around and shooting beams at anything they don't appreciate.

Data.DisplayName: The Stone Lord: A New Threat

Data.Description: The patterns in the ring's swirling metal make your head spin whenever you look at them for too long.
The sides of this brass lamp are shinier than the rest, as if they've been repeatedly rubbed.
This beetle-shaped medallion thrums with a power redolent of older civilisations in Toril - how old is this relic, all grouted with dust as it is?
Sometimes the best thing you can do for your friends is to stop bleeding and give them a chance to sort everything out.
One of Blood Vendor Araj Obladra's elixirs, distilled from a specific sanguine quality, and with properties aligned to an equally specific race.
Data.TechnicalDescription: Dwarven blood lets you add your <LSTag Tooltip="ProficiencyBonus">Proficiency Bonus</LSTag> to <LSTag Tooltip="SavingThrow">Saving Throws</LSTag> until you succeed on 3 of them or take a <LSTag Tooltip="LongRest">Long Rest</LSTag>.

Data.Description: Pages of worshipful psalms and prayers dedicated to the Lady of Silver.
An elaborate key plated with silver. It will open most doors in Moonrise Towers.
Penned in the flawless hand of one accustomed to asking for things in writing.

Wielded by Balduran, the founder of Baldur's Gate and friend to his guardian dragon, a great glittering wyrm called Ansur. Fellowship can be undone, though, as easily as you or I might unlace the strings of our shoes, and it was in a time of skullduggery and hardship that Balduran killed Ansur, carrying out the deed with this sword.

Data.DisplayName: Glory to the House of Oblodra

Data.Description: Woven with as much toughened cobweb as cloth.
Sheet music for a jaunty bardic tune.
The grip of darkness is a fear felt by many. The grip of a Dark Justiciar's gauntlets is a sacred fear reserved for an unfortunate few.

Shar's aspect winds its way through the patterns and pauldrons of this half plate, and any light cast nearby seems to almost quiver away from it, afraid. For even the light knows that the clank of this armour is swiftly followed by a Dark Justiciar's silent blade.
This book is redolent with the enticing smell of paper and ink.

Data.DisplayName: A Modest Guide To Sword Coast Wine

Data.Description: This light, curved blade is as unsusual and unforgiving as the darkness it strikes from.

Data.DisplayName: Out of the Sausage Tube Into The Shadow

Data.Description: Eldritch sigils seem to coarse through the metalwork on this amulet.
The string of this crossbow, secured tightly against the stock, came from the lyre of a powerful bard who gave up his days as a magical minstrel for a more ascetic life.
Created by a conglomerate of druids one moonlit night when all the stirring violins of insect, elms, and whispering winds consorted, and when wild beasts in need of taming prowled unseen.
This longbow was forged from the remnants of Stanislav the Silver's shield, found near the wreckage of Castle Ravenloft some years ago.
'What moves faster, a loosed crossbow bolt or a windblown cinder? Let's find out.' - Overheard during a Flaming Fist raid in Baldur's Gate.
A business document describing a deal with an important customer.
'The thing that you poor sods simply cannot grasp is how effortless all this magical hootie-wootie castie-spellsie business is for me!' - A very stupid sorcerer at a wizard academy ball.

Data.DisplayName: The Apprentice's Companion, Book the Second

Data.Description: The blade is sharp, and the handle firm. Yet death exudes from this dagger as it might from a fresh corpse.
There's a graceful swarthiness to this sword. The inscription in the steel reads - 'My eye wanders far from home / To shores of distant Anchorome.'
A note found on the decapitated corpse of a man in the Lower City.

Data.DisplayName: Open Call for Adventurers on Behalf of the Society

Data.Description: Create a surface of blood.
A paralysing eyestalk harvested from a beholder was boiled in a broth, and poured down the throat of a dwarven ringsmith. Not one fortnight thence, he crafted this ring.
Divine runes accentuate the finger pads. While not a religious sect, the Harpers do not demand the occlusion of religion in their members.
This blade is one of a few rare swords wielded by the Eucalyptus League, a group of fabulously wealthy courtesans who owned a great deal of Luskan's bazaars.

Carixim, soul-stuffed forgemaster of hellish Avernus, hammers away ceaselessly at new creations. Questions of morality and destiny do not concern him. Conscience is for his betters. He works with cheer, his swollen skin moaning soothingly.
An unofficial record of taxes collected by the Reithwin tollhouse.
When this axe careens through the air toward an unfortunate head - the whistle of its spiritual counterpart is never far behind.

The scholar of love, Joel Firris Baldidims, writes that the next time he reads about a woman compared to a flower (or any feature of geography for that matter) he's going to start knocking on poets' doors with a sledgehammer.
Sharp juts and knobbly nodules of bone stud this armour, as if something ancient sank its teeth deep into the leather and they got stuck there.

The gem in this collar's centre is placed as a common courtesy: it allows the tressym's summoner to be identified and complained to in the case of bereaved pet owners or pigeon-masters. This one glows with a Waterdhavian name: Gale Dekarios.
The golden plate glows softly, as if reflecting an inner light.

Kereska, draconic goddess of arcane knowledge, imbues many chromatic dragons with their magic. This includes their exquisite and terrible breath, which has wrenched giants from their tall thrones, and destroyed civilisations of smallfolk.

Gontr Mael blasted from the corpse of the Steelwatcher Titan: a bow formed from the boiling slag and weird whispering gyros inherent to the mechanical giant. It must have acted as the Titan's abdomen, exchanging muscle for immaculate steel.
A school notebook filled with scribblings ranging from a youth's fanciful musings to an adult's disciplined records.

Data.DisplayName: You've Got Friends in the Guild

Data.Description: A club with nails hammered through it. Classic.
Demons will bite their masters, slaves, comrades, and, on occasion, themselves. They bite on principle, and are functionally piranha with extra steps.
This selection of face-paints transform the applicant into a vibrant clown, as if by magic.
Formerly worn by Doubleway Douglas Fairbanks, who was so ambidextrous his tears ran down the back of his neck.
A purpose-made diary filled with childish scribbles and notes.
A favourite among fleet-footed gish, this cloak allows the wearer to wield a foe's elemental mastery against them.

Data.DisplayName: Wine Cart - smells of cloves and soft summer nights

Data.Description: You see... *hic* the thing... the really, really important thing *hic*... about this item is *belches copiously*... oh sod it, it's a club. Enjoy.
An agoraphobic and cantankerous traveller's journal.
The red haired man, newly freed from persecution, ambles out of amidst the bustling street coquettishly.
This loyal axe always returns to its owner after being thrown. However, it has no eyes and therefore dreadful aim, inevitably returing to its thrower blade-end-first.
This stone disc is carved with circular runes and pictographs.
Fingers of shadow seem to beckon from the dark edge of the blade.

Duke Ravengard's father was the sort of man who works with his hands, and communicates in grunts. In his heart his son vowed to do better. But when Wyll was born, Ravengard felt a strange gravity that drew him away from his son.
This ring carries the symbol of the Szarr family and has an inscription in some crusty old language.

After she returned from her confinement at the hands of the demon prince Graz'zt, the Goddess of prosperity, Waukeen, appointed a champion, who donned this studded leather and took up arms against those who had schismed and corrupted her church in the interim.
Llena the Many-Times-Married would use these gloves to blend in with the statues in her courtyard. This would allow her to avoid her plethora of husbands. Anything for a moment's peace.
Precise infernal runes are woven into this weapon's filigree, implying a creator well-versed in hellish arcana.
Based on a mad alchemist's experiments to derive youth from his victims by poisoning them, this cloak relies on a much more reliable arcane formula.
Clothing doesn't tend to have much personality. That comes down to how it's worn. Yet these gloves exude a confidence, an intangible aura of expertise.

When the boy was seven, he was frightened badly by a vampire spawn during a public burning. Seized by the flames, the creature didn't shrivel up. It swelled and burst like a squeezed leech. Brains splattered the boy's shoes, grey-pink and pulpy.

He would never forget it.
Practical jokes with these boots often involve all your stuff being stolen by opportunistic cousins.
Data.TechnicalDescription: These boots allow the wearer to cast <LSTag Type="Spell" Tooltip="Target_FeignDeath">Feign Death</LSTag> once per <LSTag Tooltip="ShortRest">Short Rest</LSTag>.

Data.Description: A hand-written note, mysterious in its intention
This staple of any worthwhile exorcist burns with a pale flame that destroys the anchors of troublesome ghosts in need of banishment.
Though thin and delicate-looking, the amulet's pendant sits heavy against your chest.
As heavy and opposed to nonsense as the wearied hammer of a sentencing magistrate.

Kereska, the draconic goddess of arcane knowledge, gifted this glaive to a dragonborn when facing off against a group of carbuncular spiders. How their arachnid legs curled and blackened before that night's dark business was done!
You get the eerie feeling that the jewelsmith used more than alien metals to forge this circlet - something like ancient magic, or shards of a soul.
This chest bears the faint likeness of six noble figures from a far-off, near-mythical land.
With every rustle of this cloak, small moths like windblown embers appear around you - they flutter for a moment, then fade into inconsequence.

One of the relics of Deep Duerra's rebellious children. Keeping themselves and one another safe from the nasty surprises of their home, the siblings made good progress.

At the final hurdle, they were confronted by none other than Duerra herself, and her rage was great, and they felt the candles of hope in their hearts snuff out.
The fire engulfing this staff seems to feed off thin air, never once burning the dark wood.
A glowering mercenary occupies this portrait - the artist has rendered his pained yet compassionate gaze in devastating detail.
An elaborate key dovetailed in silver twists. It will open most doors in Moonrise Towers.
Passed from hand to hand by those who hunt creatures from beyond the Material Plane, this flail has two words scrawled on it: 'No Trespassing.'
Local rumour claims a devil's tear gives these city militia shields their fire - much to the chagrin of the barracks blacksmith.

One of the relics of Deep Duerra's rebellious children. Long ago in a foreboding realm called Hammergrim, Deep Duerra, daughter of the dour god Laduguer, sired a great many heirs to her twisted corundum throne.

Data.DisplayName: Needle's Points: Tips for Top Stories

Data.Description: Precise infernal runes are woven into this weapon's filigree, implying a creator well-versed in hellish arcana.

Data.DisplayName: The Glitter Gala - Glittering Baldur's Gate for over Twenty Years
Note to All Knights of the Shield members

Data.Description: 'If your foe rains down blows upon your head, turn not the other cheek, but let your pricking helm bleed the bastards dry.'
Considered sacred by some gnomes and halflings, the gem set in this ring sparkles brilliantly.

Data.DisplayName:
Shield Steward Interrogation Log
Scroll or letter

Data.Description: This sacred elven blade once belonged to Ketheric Thorm. Selûne's blessing shines silver along its cutting edge.

Sent by Lathander, the god of creativity and sunrises. Unfortunately, it was not received by the cleric who needed it at that crucial moment, but by a baffled librarian in Daggerford, who used it as a door stopper.
A ring that has been robbed of its gemstone.

'And with her arm the dryad linked a man who had once been her lover, and once of flesh and bone. Now his flesh was bark, and his bone heartwood. In his eyes a feverish love still blazed like a thousand fireflies in a spring meadow.'
Embroidered with little ducks.
A whitered and hollowed head, mouth agape. Its lips are dragged down by rotten heavy jowls.
It's unclear if Kurwin was a very resourceful adventure, or just a really bad doctor.
This stone once belonged to Gortash, and is one of three controllers of the Crown of Karsus.

Data.DisplayName: House Rules of the Bee Hive

Data.Description: Even in the brightest light, this ring never gleams, as if perpetually wrapped in shadow, hungry for the dark.
Whispers in the Deep Speech of the Underdark insinuate themselves into the mind of whoever so much as brushes against the burnished metal of this ring.

This armour drips with dark ambition - the ambition of a failed godchild: Sarevok, spawn of Bhaal. Sarevok has not been remembered fondly by most historians, who almost unanimously agree that he had the general disposition of a sledgehammer.
The wind seems to lap encouragingly at the heels of these boots, no matter which direction they take.
This exquisite whiskey's most notable feature was a wyvern's scale floating in every bottle.
An elaborately gilded key.

Data.DisplayName: Harping By Moonlight: An Approach To Life

Data.Description: An shiny, deceptively simple band, designed to look like those worn by battlefield scouts and city pickpockets alike.
One cat missing. One heartfelt plea. One reward offered.
'Let your lips turn black as night/On this eve of frightful wights/Let your throat be filled with screams/Nearby looms the Raven Queen!' - A song of dark festivity

The large chunk of amber set into the handle of this luminous mace supposedly holds four drops of godly blood, fallen to the earth in a battle between an avatar of Lathander and a maddened Chosen of Mystra.
Summon Boo
Ways of beginning a duel have varied over the years. Perhaps the most famous is the Bildumbacher Method, in which the instigator drips paint thinner onto the opponent's socks.
A web of veins runs the length of the blade - it has become a slender iron mortuary for all the innocents it has tasted.
A blank master print block.
Sorcerers operate on a first-come, first-blasted basis.
Spongy purple growths, slimed with residue.
Chiselled into the back of the amulet with great care: 'sorcery > wizardry'.
A pile of today's issues of the Baldur's Mouth Gazette.
This stone once belonged to Ketheric Thorm, and is one of three controllers of the Crown of Karsus.
Wielded by the indomitable Ser Lexia. Although her eagerness to destroy evil in all its forms was constant, she often took time to make little gifts for her friends.
This lightweight armour appears to have been quickly produced, skipped stitches and fraying edges betraying the inattention of its maker.
This length of yew was polished in a lacquer made from the mingled, cooled, and refined breath of a gold and silver dragon.

These shoes were formerly enchanted to return to their owner's feet. This caused a great deal of trouble for owners, who, while wearing a slipper or a nice heeled number, kept being kicked in the ankles by jealous footwear.

Steadfast Edwina of Icewind Dale wielded this maul for many years before pursuing her desired career of fiction writing. She wrote crime novels set in Waterdeep for thirty years, and died largely unrecognised. But happy.
The inlaid jewels are so rich in colour, so deep in hue, you could lose yourself in them.
Data.TechnicalDescription: Allows you to cast Charm Person once per short rest

Data.Description: A pelvis, sundered from the rest of the body, still clothed in the stained tatters of a clown costume.
The grimy scroll includes a child's drawing of their fluffy friend.
One of Blood Vendor Araj Obladra's elixirs, distilled from a specific sanguine quality, and with properties aligned to an equally specific race.
Data.TechnicalDescription: Noble elven blood grants you an additional 10m movement speed, <LSTag Type="Passive" Tooltip="SuperiorDarkvision">Darkvision</LSTag>, and you can't be <LSTag Type="Status" Tooltip="CHARMED">Charmed</LSTag> until your next <LSTag Tooltip="LongRest">Long Rest</LSTag>.

Data.Description: A message to Kith'rak Voss from an unknown contact suggesting a meeting in Baldur's Gate.
One of Blood Vendor Araj Obladra's elixirs, distilled from a specific sanguine quality, and with properties aligned to an equally specific race.
Data.TechnicalDescription: You can call on diabolic arcana to cast <LSTag Type="Spell" Tooltip="Shout_Thaumaturgy">Thaumaturgy</LSTag>, <LSTag Type="Spell" Tooltip="Shout_HellishRebuke">Hellish Rebuke</LSTag>, <LSTag Type="Spell" Tooltip="Zone_BurningHands">Burning Hands</LSTag>, and <LSTag Type="Spell" Tooltip="Shout_FlameBlade">Flame Blade</LSTag> each only once until your next <LSTag Tooltip="LongRest">Long Rest</LSTag>.

Data.Description: The mysterious gem set in this ring seems to change hues whenever you aren't looking.
This simple cured goat hide was enchanted by a travelling druid. A goatherd once helped her negotiate a strange maze of hedges, so she blessed all his goats in thanks.
Supplies power to the House of Hope.
Indigo cloth manipulated into elaborate patterns mark this outfit's wearer as a gregarious observer, listener, and conversationalist.
The slightest movement of leather makes a dark energy seep out of the gloves.
A leafy pattern is carved into the dagger's blade. It glows faintly in the dark.
The red haired man languishes in prison, guarded by cruel buffoons.
Revenge is best served. Hot or cold makes no difference.
The taut violet leather is drier than snakeskin, and puckered at each knuckle with shallow mouth-shaped pits.
Why does it smell like a herb garden?

Data.DisplayName: Eternal Carafe of Wine (Or Sometimes Acid)
Data.Description: Each morning, this carafe refills with wine. Sometimes, however, instead of wine, it refills with indigestible acid.
Conducting a series of increasingly sick rituals - involving the ashes of a gnome and silkworms fed fat on the corpse of a dwarven cleric - the goblin shaman Kirruk Redrats created this deadly bow.
The anonymous liquid in this draft is not viscous but moves with an unusual lethargy when tilted.
Every contract a devil makes has some form of insurance - this one is cast in infernal iron and was forged in deep, ruinous hellfire.

Any tales about the Paladins of Velen are so ancient as to be almost certainly hearsay. Irrefutable, however, is the powerful blessing they left on this ancient shield, which inspires heart-fluttering bravery to this day.

Timid, god-fearing Cat Burroughs was dizzyingly happy when an angel courted her one summer. But in the autumn, when he shamefacedly revealed he was not an angel but an incubus of the Hells, Cat flew into a rage, slew him, and fashioned this armour from his wings and still-warm bones.

Data.DisplayName: Opportunity to work with a master artisan

Data.Description: It's never the shield that kills you - but hearing your frantic steel thudding uselessly against this reinforced oak in the darkness is a good sign the end is near.
Supple and strong, this shortbow has been imbued with a ranger's solemn magic - running your fingers along the smooth ash, you can feel that solemnity like a ghost in the shaped wood.
The bark motifs in this armour are like the boles of oak trees in a wood where the acorns slept long, and grew proud.
Though vindictive and about as kindly as a tsunami, Umberlee the Sea Goddess is occasionally inclined toward restorative acts, as gentle as placid waves on a white-gold shore.
Many an adventurer has found themselves swallowed up by the dark throat of some nameless dungeon, aching for a glimpse of light.
So much power, a gateway to become a Mind Flayer.
The wielder of this rod cannot be <LSTag Type="Status" Tooltip="SURPRISED">Surprised</LSTag>, unless something unexpected happens.
When on the wrong side of a few sherries, the powerful wizards Bigby and Tenser would sometimes see how many spells they could fit into amulets like this one before they burst.

Data.DisplayName: Beating the House: Divination and Gambling

Data.Description: This otherwise unassuming ring ties a spellcaster indelibly to the sporadic arcana of the Faerie realm.
Flowing through your chest, threads of whiskey-like warmth - they spread and spread, and who could lay you low, you champion in hopeful hours?

Data.DisplayName: Ribald Shanties for the Discerning Whoreson

Data.Description: Raw Sun Crystal

Data.DisplayName: Stock Display: A Primer, by Sana Aeran
Data.Description: A shopkeepers' manual on how to display merchandise to maximum effect.

Data.DisplayName: Concerning the Future of Baldur's Gate

Data.Description: An invitation to Baldur's Gate's book club, addressed to Nansi.
In the steel, you can see small ice formations like bubbles in a bath, and even hear them pop with crickling crackles of frosted delight.
Stitched into the fabric of these gloves are the words: Largest and Largesse, For The Discerning Murderer.
Blood enthrals and holds great dominion over people. Its wine-dark stain anoints even the pacifist in such troubled times as these.
Droplets of foul acid drip from the tails of this cloak, as if from the stinger of a demonic scorpion.
The tourmaline in this necklace is almost uncomfortably hot, warmed by a heat all its own.
Ash dusts the gloves' fingers, darkening their seams.

Long ago, Kushigo was a warrior. Bedecked in an enormous set of plate steel, its shoulder pauldrons fashioned like great antlered stags, his arrival on a battlefield spelled doom for the enemy.

Yet this armour - so light and fine - speaks nothing to that legacy.
A Lulutiun hand drum covered in sealskin, like those played at koatulit peace festivals. Kiam Goda was famous for his finger-thumb taradiddles.
This teddy bear toy is stuffed with explosives. Still adorable.
This decanter can, in fact, sometimes run out endless water. However, it will definitely regain its properties next day. The day after, for sure.
A small iron key.
A strong paralytic poison.

Data.DisplayName: The Time of the Patriars is Over!

Data.Description: What precisely confers eternal punishment, reward, absolution? Perhaps it's not just belief in a god. Perhaps the deciding factor is whether the gods believe in you.
The ruby's red reflections look like eerie flames dancing across your skin.
Worn by a scoundrel of the lowest morals and the highest cunning.
Heavy steel bones and teeth enclose the armour's chest and neck like a grotesque exoskeleton that both swallows and protects the wearer.
A scrap of paper splattered in blood, and other bodily fluids.

Earnest little Edith Cluckle was a small girl when she asked to be the great wizard Otiluke's apprentice. He scoffed at her, but was quickly abashed when Mystra herself endowed Edith with this very cloak.

Data.DisplayName: The One that Got A Thay

Data.Description: A hunk of fetid Dalelands Blue. Looks putrid. Smells even worse.

When the Lord of Murder, Bhaal, was rendered mortal, he knew his days were numbered. His vile machinations had gained him many enemies.

Those days ran out and Bhaal was indeed killed, not by a god, but by a man with hawkish features named Cyric.
A grudging gleam emits from this ring - more an indictment of light than an endorsement.
A series of motivational quotes have been enthusiastically removed from the embroidery of these gloves, as if in protest.
Rough and coarse, the cloak's materials soften to silk when immersed in shadow.

Data.DisplayName: The Layperson's Guide To Holy Exorcism
For The Discerning Eyes of Oskar Fervas ONLY

Data.Description: The soft hum of power emanates from the alien metal.
An old issue of the Baldur's Mouth Gazette.

A garment worn by one of three monks who fought together against Headless Serpent, Secret Venom, a gang in the port city of Nyanzaru. This was worn by Roahton Mobar, whose stances were broad and strong.

These boots are heavy and slow to step in - perhaps due to the gargoyle spirit reportedly trapped within. While that legend's truth is debatable, the protection these boots offer against toe-stubbing is not.
Dents, notches, and nicks add character to each ring of this mail - yet each blemish also speaks to those who tasted magical vengeance on the armour's behalf.
Etchings course red-hot through the length of this staff, the script of primordial fire writ in flame.

Presumably Mizora was not always a sensuous and manipulative benefactor of troubled souls like Wyll. Negotiating the hierarchies of hell result in changes of form - but was she ever less beautiful, less erudite, less willful?
This stone disc is carved with circular runes and pictographs.
Where once this shield would protect the rallying forces of good - now it pushes them back, crushing them against their allies until they pop.
If pants could brood...
One of Blood Vendor Araj Obladra's elixirs, distilled from a specific sanguine quality, and with properties aligned to an equally specific race.
Data.TechnicalDescription: When you are <LSTag Tooltip="Downed">Downed</LSTag> before your next <LSTag Tooltip="LongRest">Long Rest</LSTag>, you instead drop to 1 hit point thanks to the relentless will roiling in your veins.

Data.Description: A key to the front door of Candulhallow's Tombstone Shop.
The gemstone centrepiece of the amulet was long ago mottled and dyed by the tears of a martyr.
Donning this necklace causes the room to sway and tip - or maybe it was already swaying? Whatever, time for another pint.

'Beneath those horrible sounds of... well, let's call it what it was: torment, Beneath the tormented screams I heard this moaning sound like many people in pain, and I heard the ringing of a great hammer. Carixim's forge was close.' - Overheard from the smith Dammon
Look no further than Scyllua Darkhope - fallen paladin and champion of Bane - to see how the tools of good can be turned to evil purpose.

Data.DisplayName: Control panel with a unique slot.
Data.Description: A workbench, its surfaces warped, scorched, burnished, and even hardened with the proximity of such fervent toil.
Gyldro Angleiron's journal.
One of Blood Vendor Araj Obladra's elixirs, distilled from a specific sanguine quality, and with properties aligned to an equally specific race.
Data.TechnicalDescription: You have <LSTag Tooltip="Advantage">Advantage</LSTag> on Intimidation and Persuasion <LSTag Tooltip="AbilityCheck">Checks</LSTag>, <LSTag Tooltip="Resistant">Resistance</LSTag> to Lightning damage, and can use <LSTag Type="Spell" Tooltip="Zone_MOO_BloodPotion_LightningBolt">Lightning Bolt</LSTag> once until your next <LSTag Tooltip="LongRest">Long Rest</LSTag>.

Data.DisplayName: The House on Drench Lane and Other Stories

Data.Description: Designed by gnomish innovation, this weapon has a dynamic core that swivels and tinkles into life whenever the axe is swung at a foe.
Likely fashioned in tribute to the extremely small, high-vaulting rascal who pillaged many a hen house - Lupperdiddle Swires.
A leg, slit and sundered, flaked with clown makeup and garbed in the pastels of the circus.

Data.DisplayName: Fine at Home: A Cookery Book

Data.Description: Deals Fire and Thunder damage to nearby objects and knocks them back.
Some scholars have speculated that spells have a mind of their own, suggesting that the spells get bored between being cast and restored.
Smelling of long-abandoned gardens grown wild with thorny roses, moss and hibiscus, this armour was worn by a powerful druid who spent so long from people that she forgot to miss them.

This staff was wielded by Thibault Hollow, a supremely talented necromancer notable for his overwhelming fear of zombies. Many was the time when his dread lair would echo with a high-pitched shriek when one of them surprised him in a corridor, or when he was taking a bath.
An old issue of the Baldur's Mouth Gazette.
A shopkeeper's ledger of products, clients, and quantities. It smells pleasantly of explosive powder.
This stone once belonged to Orin, and is one of three controllers of the Crown of Karsus.

Clad on the desiccated feet of a death knight, these boots have walked a long and terrible path. They strode through the tattered remains of their owner's oath. With every heavy footstep, they have sounded pure fear into the hearts of men.
Nightsong's armour is evocative of her personality - prickly, hardy, and about as agreeable as a clenched fist.
No ore takes better to being forged than the infernal iron of Avernus, where the archdevil Zariel presides.
A filled in print block.

Fashioned by some unknown archmage - no identifying insignia is forthcoming.

The staff thrums with a slow, ferocious pulse that draws its concussive power from the spiral-horned creatures that gave the weapon its name.
A simple bag, loosely tied.
A noble warrior's cloak, woven in the heart of an ancient empire.

The most pragmatic and courageous lover ever known was, of course, Sorcha MacTire, for whom the popular hairstyle is named, and for whom many an extremely soppy poem has been written (most of them comparing her to geography).

Listening to the magical hum this robe emits dulls your senses, thoughts, feelings - everything. Listen too long, and you can almost hear the screaming chitters of a thousand spiders devoured by encroaching, hungry darkness. Almost.
This charming piece's hue reminds of the flower often sprouting from anonymous graves.

Formerly worn by Autumnal Baskin, a professional meditator turned bare-knuckle champion, who gained enlightenment via two methods. The first was giving up her addictive reliance on secluded caves and lonely mountaintops, and getting a bit more sociable. This involved many new skirts. Most of them lavender.
A psionic crystal that fits into a githyanki barrier disruptor to suppress nearby energy fields.
The impression of an elven face screams silently from the finely curved bow - the image becomes even more disturbing when the bowstring snaps forward on release, emitting a blood-curdling wail.
For some, darkness is wielded like a black opal stud embedded in a signet ring - fashioned to a sharp and unforgiving point.
A foot, bruised and bloody, flaked with clown makeup and garbed in the pastels of the circus.

Data.DisplayName: To the Flaming Fist Duty Officer

Data.Description: Formerly worn by Autumnal Baskin, a professional meditator turned bare-knuckle champion, who gained enlightenment via two methods. The second was getting a lot of fighting acumen. Advanced cosmic harmony is a nose. Sometimes you've got to break it a few times to get the best of things.
Designed for the jobbing spellcaster, these gloves are well-insulated to prevent digit immolation for the somatically inept.
A tattered book of drawings, stained with wine and reeking of bodily fluids of all sorts.
Reliable and trustworthy, you could not hope for more respectable company than this maul whilst traversing the forlorn places of the world.
A loosely bound collection of notes and diagrams.
The Parliament of Peers' official approval of Gortash as Archduke of Baldur's Gate.

This mace was designed by Lolth's assassins to fell heretics who dared turn their back on the Spider Queen. However, even the best-laid designs fall to nothingness when brought to bear against Shar's faithful.
Handed out to all students during orientation at the arcane universities of the world. However, a bit of enchanted cloth is a meagre defence against one's classmates.
In his speculative writing on arcane displacement, the wizard Tenser notes the possibility for keenly focused minds to maintain spells, and even unlock hidden potential while doing so.
An elaborate key, plated with silver.
The soft hum of a fervent prayer reverberates throughout the armoured plates.
Through a gap in the long snarls of thread, you are sure you can glimpse a great black thunderhead swollen with purple lightning and spears of rain.
Strange, green fumes seep from the ring's emerald.
A summary of the events at the start of Murder In Baldur's Gate.
A hacked-off arm, still sporting the brightly coloured sleeve of a circus clown's costume.
Zhentarim spies have been known to take on the aspect of the phasmid - an insect sometimes called the devil's darning needle - to blend into their surroundings.
Thou shalt not suffer a witch to... well, keep doing whatever she's doing. It's probably malefic, involving toads and... and things.
A plain, unadorned note.

It's certainly possible that there are sadder things than decimated cabbage. It's just that, looking at the bruised leaves adrip with still-warm manure, one finds it difficult to remember what they might be exactly.

Data.DisplayName: A Study of Spores and their Supraterranean Effects

Data.Description: We see the red haired thief upon a swiftly erected gallows, his face aggrieved.
Balling your fingers into fists while wearing these gloves causes a sonorous chime, like the fusion of a tempest and a church bell, to resound inside your skull.
On the stock, the crafter of this crossbow etched in tiny print: 'Ifn yer gonna miss, why dontchyae stop being a wally, and hit instead!'
Formerly the property of the royalty of Threskel, these gauntlets impart some of the prince of Threskel's legendary skill with weapons.
Encased in a cocoon of shadow within the lantern, the mangled pixie lies like some deformed pupa, its mouth slack, and those same shadows crawling over its graying tongue.
The sting of fear at the encroachment of some hulking brute is lessened by these gloves. In fact, in such moments, they send rivulets of courage coursing through you.
These gloves smell like beef mince left to rot in a privy pail.
To hold this shield is to be vigilant in duty, wary of danger, and mindful in crisis.
'Beneath the tormented screams, I heard this moaning sound like many people in pain, and I heard the ringing of a great hammer. Carixim's forge was close.' - Overheard from the smith Dammon

A reward received from biting Araj Oblodra. Vampirism has sometimes been called The Dark Gift, or the Dark Kiss, perhaps as an allusion to their forbidden relationship to sunshine. It does provide gifts in abundance; such is the case with this potion.
Data.TechnicalDescription: Permanently increase your <LSTag Tooltip="Strength">Strength</LSTag> by 2.

Data.Description: Yes, but what exactly is hitting you?

Because it was designed by a compulsive mumbler, this staff can't distinguish between its spells, and so can only cast - <LSTag Type="Spell" Tooltip="Projectile_Fireball">Fireball</LSTag> or <LSTag Type="Spell" Tooltip="Target_Firebolt">Firebolt</LSTag> at random.
The ring is scuffed and twisted out of shape, as if worn by big stony fingers. The owner of those fingers has carved 'Karthol' into the warped metal in a fit of affection or possessiveness.
Plant your feet firm as an oak, your roots determinate, your balance as precise as the contour of the moon.
A plain, unadorned note.
Dark and suitably moody, these gloves are perfect for wearing while thinking about poetry.
A treatise by Cristina Suelto proposing harsh retaliation against political adversaries.
This flail was created to commemorate victory over the devil Belhifet. It has since made its way so far from Easthaven that the locals have long forgotten that chapter of their town's past.

The gentle tap-tap-tap of a staff on stone sparked terror for all in Cazador's palace. It signalled an approaching storm, and all they could do was shrink into the background and pray its wrath would not fall on them.

The leather grip of this knife is decorated with jugs. As you turn it, you can see that the jug begins empty and fills.

It's only when you reach the final image that you can see a man's severed head held over the jug, filling it with beads of blood.
A near-perfect relic that is only blemished by the collected palm-sweat of various archmagi from across the Realms.
Tyr is often known as the Maimed God - a descriptor he shares with most victims of this heavy warhammer.
Llena the Many-Times-Married would use these gloves to blend in with the statues in her courtyard. This would allow her to avoid her plethora of husbands. Anything for a moment's peace.
A yellowed but crisp note; it appears to have been written some years ago, but not often read.
Official revocation of Counsellor Florrick's authority over the Flaming Fist.
This potion of sleep is empty.
A coldness clings to this macabre circlet, like the chill of a grave.
This axe is so loyal, it will sometimes return to wielders it favours.
